Muslims, and that is because blood and wealth, although it is desirable for the oppressed to pardon his oppressor in it, then the ruler who judges between the people, Whenever an oppressed person is judged to abandon his rights, he is judging with injustice, not with justice.

And if We ordered every guardian of a murdered person not to take revenge on the killer, and every debtor not to demand his debtor, but to leave him to his choice, and every He was reviled and smitten because he did not seek justice from his oppressor. The oppressors had no rebuke to rebuke them, and the strong oppressed the weak, and the land became corrupt. God Almighty said: {And had God not repulsed people one by another, the earth would have been corrupted} [Al-Baqarah: 251].
There must be a law that includes ruling with justice, and it must - with that - encourage people to forgive and take credit.
This is the law of Islam, as we mentioned above in the verses, such as his saying: {And wounds are retaliation, so whoever gives them in charity, it is an expiation. To Him} [Al-Ma’idah: 45].
And His saying: {And if it is a difficult situation, then look for an easy one, and if you give in charity, that is better for you} [Al-Baqarah: 280].:.
And he said: “And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it. So whoever pardons and makes amends, his reward is with Allah” [Al-Shura: 40].
And His saying: {And if you punish, then punish with the like of what you were punished with, and if you are patient - indeed, it is better for those who are patient.} [An-Nahl: 126].
And He said: “Those who spend in good times and in adversity, and who restrain anger and pardon people. And God loves the doers of good.” [Al Imran: 134].
And his saying: {A friendly animal left to its family unless they give in charity} [An-Nisa: 92]...
And he said: {And to him who is patient and forgives - indeed, that is one of the determination of matters} [Al-Shura: 43].

Anas said: “No matter was presented to the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - a matter involving retaliation, except that he ordered pardoning.” So he was commanding pardon, but not binding. people with it; For this reason, when Barira was emancipated, and she had the right to annul the marriage, and her husband asked that she not separate from him, he interceded for her not to separate from him. She said: Do you command me? He said: No, I am only an intercessor, so she was not obligated to accept his intercession - may God bless him and grant him peace.

The twelfth aspect: Their saying: “And since the perfection that is virtue cannot be achieved by anyone except the most perfect of perfection,” it is said to them: Justice and virtue are legislated by none but God. The law of the Torah was legislated by none but God, and the law of the Gospel was legislated by none but God Almighty.

This shows that God spoke to Moses from the tree, and the ultimate goal by which they affirmed the divinity of Christ was that they claimed that God spoke to the people from The humanity of Christ, just as He spoke to Moses from the tree, and it is known to every rational person, if this were true, that His speech to Moses from the tree is greater. A word that God spoke to His servants, so how can it be said: The law of justice was not legislated by God Almighty? .

Then it will be said to them: Rather, the law of justice is more deserving of being added to God than the law of grace, for the command to do good and pardon is improved by everyone. No one, and as for knowing justice and ruling among people with it, only a few people are capable of it. For this reason, there are many people who reconcile people with kindness, but as for the one who is good at separating between them with justice, there are few people. How can it be said: The one who orders the law of virtue is God, not the one who orders the law of justice? .

And God - the Almighty - sent the messengers and sent down the books. So that the people may adhere to justice, as God Almighty said: {Indeed, We have sent Our messengers with clear proofs, and We sent down with them the Book and the Balance, so that the people may With justice, and We sent down iron in it, mighty force and benefits for people, and so that God may know who will support Him and His messengers in the unseen. Indeed, God is Powerful, Mighty} [Al-Hadid: 25].

And the command of Christ - peace be upon him - to the oppressed person to pardon the oppressor: There is nothing in it that indicates that it is an obligation that whoever neglects it deserves to be blamed. Punishment is something that is desirable and that whoever does it deserves praise and reward. Moses - peace be upon him - made justice obligatory, and whoever neglected it deserved condemnation and punishment. In that case, there is no contradiction between the obligation of justice and the desirability of virtue.

But the obligation of justice is accompanied by intimidation and intimidation in abandoning it, and the desirability of virtue is accompanied by the encouragement and longing to do it. That is awe as well as desire. This contains desire without fear. That is why Christ - peace be upon him - said:.

{And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them, but when you took me to death, you were the watcher over them, and you are a witness over all things - if you punish them, it will be their fault. Your servants, and if You forgive them, it is You, the Mighty, the Wise.} [Al-Maeda: 117-118].

For this reason it was said: Christ - peace be upon him - was sent to complete the Torah, for the voluntary acts are to be performed after the obligatory ones, as in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurairah - may God be pleased with him - on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - he said: “God Almighty says:

“Whoever is hostile to a friend of mine has fought against me, and my servant will not draw near to me in the same way as I have enjoined upon him, and my slave will not continue to draw near to me.” To me to do voluntary deeds so that I may love him. If I love him, I will be his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, and his hand with which he strikes. With it, and his leg with which he walks, by me he hears and by me he sees and by me he runs and by me he walks. And if he asks of Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me I will seek refuge in Him, and I have never hesitated from anything that I would do as I hesitate to take the soul of My faithful servant. He hates death and I hate to touch him. He has it from him.”

Otherwise, if it were said: Christ - peace be upon him - made it obligatory for the oppressed to forgive the oppressor; Meaning that he deserves the threat, the blame, and the punishment if he does not pardon him. This entails that everyone who takes justice from the oppressor is an unjust. Deserving of rebuke and punishment, and this is a second injustice to the oppressed person who was treated justly. For the oppressor wronged him first, and when he did justice to him, he wronged him secondly, so he wronged the just person who did justice to his oppressor.
How beautiful are the words of God when He says:

{So whatever you have been given is the enjoyment of this worldly life, but what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and put their trust in their Lord - and those who shun Great sins and immoralities, and when they are angry, they forgive - and those who responded to their Lord and established prayer, and their affair was consultation among themselves. And of what We have provided them they spend - and those who, when transgression befalls them, retaliate - and the recompense for an evil is another evil like it - so whoever pardons. And he makes amends, his reward is with God. Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers - and whoever retaliates after his wrongdoing - those have no path - but the path is upon those who They oppress people and commit wrong in the land unjustly. For these is a painful punishment.

And he said: {That and whoever is punished with the like of what he was punished with, and then transgression is committed against him - God will certainly grant him victory. Indeed, God is indeed Pardoning and Forgiving} [Al-Hajj: 60].
This is one of the best, most just, and best of words, since He legislated justice, saying: “And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil like it” [Al-Shura: 40].
Then he called for virtue, and said: {So whoever pardons and makes amends, his reward is from Allah. Indeed, He does not love wrongdoers.} [Al-Shura: 40].

When he called for forgiveness, he mentioned that there is no blame on the one who is in the middle, lest it be thought that forgiveness is obligatory, and he said: {And for whoever takes revenge after his injustice. Those are the ones who have no way.} [Al-Shura: 41].

Then he made it clear that the path is only upon the wrongdoers, and he said: {The path is only upon those who oppress people and transgress unjustly in the land. Those are For them is a painful punishment} [Al-Shura: 42].
Then, when He cleared the path for them, He urged them to be patient and forgiving, and said:
{And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the determination of matters} [Al-Shura: 43].

This is the best and wisest law, which encourages patience, forgiveness, forgiveness, and reconciliation with the aim of encouraging, and mentions the virtues it contains. And good deeds and Praiseworthy of the outcome, and He removes the blame from the one who wronged him and pardons him, and makes it clear that there is no blame on him and no recourse if He was victorious after being wronged.
Is it possible for a law to come that provides a path for the just person with his justice, while it does not provide a path for the oppressor with his injustice? .

So it was known that what Christ commanded regarding pardon was not because the one who abandoned it was deserving of blame and punishment, but rather because he was deprived of what the healthy person gets. The doer of good will receive reward and reward, and this is a right that does not contradict the law of the Torah. It is known that the law of the Gospel did not contradict the law of the Torah. Since it was a branch of it and a complement to it, and at that time their claim that the law of the Gospel was legislated by God without the law of the Torah is the words of an ignorant person. People and led them astray, and for this reason it was an offshoot of their statement of unity, and that Christ is God.
That is the misguidance that led to this impossible statement.

chapters.title: Chapter on the invalidity of their reasoning from what they claim to be from the words of previous prophets
paragraphs: [Chapter: The invalidity of their evidence based on what they claim is from the words of previous prophets]

A chapter and all that they used as evidence from the Torah, the Gospel, and other words of the prophets - peace be upon them - the argument for it is only scientific. Demonstratively, if they established evidence for the prophecy of the one whose words they used as evidence, by showing the possibility of prophecy and then showing its occurrence in the specific person. In the ways in which the Prophet’s prophecy is proven.

They did not do any of that, but rather they used that as an excuse based on the fact that it was an axiom given to them by the Muslims. This does not benefit them for several reasons: one of them is that among those they mentioned is someone who has not been proven by Muslims to be a prophet like Micaiah and Amoz.

Second: That whose prophethood is proven to the Muslims, such as Moses, Jesus, David, and Solomon, it is not proven to them that they said all the things they mentioned. The speech and its translation into Arabic is what they mentioned, and what they meant by it is what they interpreted.

Third: The majority of Muslims do not know the prophecy of any of the prophets before Muhammad except through information from Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace. With their prophecy, they cannot believe in the prophecy of any of these people except after believing in the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

If these people asked the Muslims to surrender the prophecy of these people, without the prophecy of Muhammad, the Muslims could not surrender that to them, nor This is permissible for Muslims, neither by reason nor by tradition, and then if they do not establish evidence of the prophethood of those people; They did not mention either a demonstrative argument or a dialectical argument.

Fourth: The Muslims did not believe in the prophecy of Moses and Jesus, unless they were informed of the prophecy of Muhammad. If they accepted that they were informed of the prophecy of Muhammad's prophethood and theirs have been proven, and if they deny that, the Muslims will deny the prophethood of those who claim to be Moses.
And Jesus, who were not informed about Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

Fifth: It is forbidden for Muslims and every sane person - after full consideration - to acknowledge the prophecy of Moses and Jesus rather than Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace -, since His prophecy was more complete, and the methods of knowing it were more complete and more complete, and there is no evidence that can be used to prove the prophecy of anyone else except that it is more evidence of his own prophecy. Denying his own prophecy entails denying the prophecy of others in the same way. But whoever said that is contradictory, just as all the people of falsehood are contradictory. For this reason, God Almighty said regarding the disbelievers: “Indeed, you are of differing speech, from which one who is more eloquent will be turned away from it” [Al-Dhariyat: 8].

chapters.title: A chapter on proving the credit to the Messenger of God, his law, and his nation
paragraphs: [Chapter: Proving the credit to the Messenger of God, to his law, and to his nation]

A chapter in which we mentioned in the answer to the beginning of their letter an explanation of their refusal to invoke any of the words of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - or anyone else. The Prophets - peace be upon them - on whatever of their religion is contrary to the religion of the Muslims. We will simplify this here and say: There is no doubt that falsehood is not supported by sound evidence, neither rational nor legitimate. Whether it is news or requests.

Valid evidence necessitates the validity of what is indicated by it. If there is valid evidence against falsehood, it must be true even though it is false, and that is A combination of the two opposites; Such as the fact that something exists and does not exist.

The People of the Book have truth in the information and requests, and with them there is falsehood, which is what they have changed in the information, regardless of whether the change is The word or its meaning and what they invented or what processes were abrogated. The manuscripts in which the laws varied are few in comparison to what the books and messengers agreed upon. What they agreed upon is what is essential for creation in every time and place, which is faith in God, the Last Day, and good deeds. As God Almighty said:

{Indeed, those who believe, and those who are Jews, and the Sabians, and the Christians, and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, and does righteousness, there is no fear upon them, nor shall they They grieve} [Al-Ma’idah: 69]...

In general, the Meccan surahs, such as Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, Al-Ham, Al-Tas, and Al-Ra, are among the universal principles agreed upon by the laws of Islam. Messengers, such as the command to worship God alone with no partner, truthfulness, justice, and sincerity, and the prohibition of injustice and immoral acts. And polytheism, and speaking against God without knowledge, and in general what they have of the correct narrations from the prophets from the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms. The prophecies of the prophets agree with what is reported on the authority of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - this man testified to this and this to this.
This is one of the signs of the prophecy of those prophets and one of the signs of the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace.

For this reason, God mentions that as an explanation of His blessings with Muhammad and an indication of his prophecy, as He - the Most High - said: {And when the angels said, “O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds - O Mary, be obedient to your Lord and prostrate and kneel with those who kneel - this is from the news of the unseen. We revealed it to you, and you were not with them when they cast their pens as to which of them should be responsible for Mary, and you were not with them when they disputed.} [Al Imran: 42-44].

And He said: - God Almighty - when he told the story of Noah: {These are tidings of the unseen which We have revealed to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this. So be patient. Indeed, the outcome is for the righteous.} [Hud: 49]
So God mentioned His blessing and His sign, even though neither he nor his people knew it. Lest it be thought that he learned that from his people, for his people did not know that.

It is known through reliable transmission that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was born in Mecca, and grew up there after he was breastfed in the desert of Sa’ad. Ibn Bakr, near Taif, east of Mecca, when he was young. Then his wet nurse, Halima Al-Saadia, carried him.

To his mother in Mecca, he does not know any of that, and there is no one to learn any of that from. The people of Mecca knew about his condition and that he did not learn that from anyone. Then he told them of the unseen, which no one knows except through teaching. God bless him.

This was one of the signs of his message, and evidence of his prophecy, to them first, and to others last. Because they were watching him, they knew that he did not learn that from anyone. And others know this through the repeated narrations, and they know that his people deny him, despite their eagerness to challenge him, and despite their knowledge In his case, if he had learned from the People of the Book, they would have said: This is what he learned from them. He - the Almighty - said: {Say, “If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would I have made it known to you. I have remained among you for a lifetime before it. Will you not understand?” [Yunus: 16].

What is meant is that he denied his people’s knowledge of what he told them, explaining the blessings of God, which are His signs and blessings, for this indicates that he did not He learns that from his people, and it is God’s blessings upon creation.

And He - the Almighty - said when He mentioned the story of Joseph: {This is of the tidings of the unseen which We have revealed to you, and you were not with them when they gathered their affair and were plotting} [Joseph: 102]

And God Almighty said: {And We gave Moses the Scripture after We had destroyed the first generations: insight for the people and guidance and mercy that they might remember - and what You were by the western side when We conveyed to Moses the matter, but you were not of the witnesses - but We created generations, and their lives were prolonged, and you were not vindicated. Among the people of Madinah, Our verses were recited to them, but we were messengers - and you were not by the mountain when we called, but it was a mercy from your Lord} [Al-Qasas: 43-46].

So He - Glory be to Him - denied His testimony to these absent matters and His presence in them. As a warning to the people that he was informed of the unseen that he had not witnessed or known about, in terms of informing people, his people were not They know that, and he has never lived with anyone other than his own people. Everyone who knew his condition knew that he did not learn anything from that, neither from the People of the Book nor from those who reported from the People of the Book.

So if Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - reported something like what the prophets before him reported, in the chapter on God’s names and attributes, And His monotheism, His angels, His guardians, and His enemies, knowing that there are many details regarding these matters that cannot be agreed upon. Two against him, except for collusion between them, and Muhammad and Moses - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - did not collude; in fact, Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them - did not collude. Peace and blessings of God be upon him - none of the messengers before him, nor did they have intercourse with him.
False news is either the one who reported it intentionally or made a mistake. Two liars who deliberately tell lies do not agree on long stories and great details.

Likewise, the two blunderers do not agree in such a case; rather, two people are among the same people, if each of them is told about the condition of a town. And he told the other the same news without collaborating, and he knew their truthfulness. So what about the hidden matters that cannot be known except by someone? With regard to God Almighty, this is one of the signs of the prophecy of the prophets - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them.
As for the fate that contradicts what Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought from what they transmit from the prophets, they are of two types: one of them:

Where abrogation of the laws occurs, and this does not prevent it, but what is abrogated is like this in relation to what was not abrogated from the book by its counterpart. Abrogated portions of the Qur’an and the Prophet’s hadiths, as they are very few in comparison to what was not abrogated, and likewise in general what Moses commanded. And David, the Messiah, and other prophets, if it was considered what Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - commanded, was generally found to be in agreement, it would not Only a small portion of it has been abrogated.

The second: news. Some of the People of the Book have claimed that Muhammad contradicted some of what the prophets had told him before him, and this is false, for the narrations It is not permissible for the prophets to contradict each other; Since they - all of them - are truthful and truthful, and whoever knows that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that Moses is the Messenger of God, and that Christ is the Messenger of God, knows that Their reports do not contradict each other, but this person may tell something that this person did not tell; Thus, the news of one of them contains additions to the news of others, not anything that contradicts the news of others.

Whatever the People of the Book mention that contradicts the report of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - it is - his generality - of what they have distorted its meaning and interpretation, and they are few. The word of it was distorted, and the People of the Book - Jews and Christians - and Muslims agree that the previous books were distorted, either Intentionally or by mistake in its translation, interpretation, explanation and interpretation. But people disputed: Did some of its words become distorted? And everything in which someone claims that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - contradicted it, he must prove two premises: one of them is:
That word is proven from that Prophet.
The second: its meaning is proven.

And whoever uses a narration from a prophet as evidence, he must have these two premises: the chain of transmission and the text. He must have proven wording, and he must It has the proven meaning of the word. If the transmission is not in the language of the Prophet, but in another language, then a correct translation is necessary, and Christians in general do not have the books of the Prophets. In the language of the prophets.
Moses, Christ, and all the prophets of the children of Israel spoke in the Hebrew language.

Christ was a Hebrew. He did not speak anything other than Hebrew, but rather spoke something else, such as Syriac, Greek, and Roman, some of them. Follow him. The majority of Christians do not know Hebrew, so they do not know how to read in Hebrew, neither the Torah, nor the Gospel, nor anything else. They only speak of this:

Romans, Syriacs, or others, even if there were a few among them who spoke Hebrew, unlike the Jews, then Hebrew Fascism among them, and then whoever among the People of the Book uses as evidence any of the words of the prophets transmitted in Romans, Syriac or... In Arabic, in addition to proving the transmission, it is necessary to prove the translation and its validity. They often have confusion about the translation and its accuracy, and they disagree about its meaning.

These are three introductions that they must adhere to in everything they use as evidence from the words of the prophets. And if they did not claim that it contradicts what he was told, Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - so how if they claim that it contradicts what Muhammad - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - brought? If it is estimated that it is proven that A prophet told something that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - would definitely not tell the opposite.

There is also something that was reported on the authority of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - whose wording is not consistent; Like some weak and fabricated hadiths, while his wording is proven, its meaning is not clear in the contradiction, and it does not indicate that.
How many interpret the Qur’an according to what the word of the Qur’an does not indicate, and none of the Companions, or even the Followers, said it.

Like someone who says: Shuaib the Prophet was the father-in-law of Moses. There is nothing in the Qur’an, the Sunnah, and the words of the Companions except what indicates the opposite of that. It is as if he said: The messengers who were sent to the village were followers of Christ. There is nothing in the Qur’an and what is transmitted from the Companions except what indicates the opposite of that.

As for what it is known that Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - told, there has been conclusive and certain evidence of his truthfulness and the truth of what he told. With it, it is greater than what it was based on the truthfulness of others and the truthfulness of what he brought, so no matter what opposes that, it is known that it is a lie to the prophets. It is not possible for any of humanity to cite definitive proof of the authenticity of that transmission. Rather, their goal is to mention a speculative path that will only benefit them. Suspicion, and suspicion does not contradict certainty.
Whatever Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - brought, the one who has reasoned and reasoned can know it with certainty and without doubt.

Whatever contradicts it, there is no way for anyone to know it, and it is inconceivable that he could follow it in his heart except suspicion and imitation, and neither of them contradicts it. Knowledge, this is a comprehensive principle. Then the knower expresses it with each person according to what conveys its meaning to that addressee. What is meant here is to say: Everything they use as evidence that contradicts what has been proven from Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - cannot be done for them. There is evidence for this that is neither legal nor rational, and we know this in general.

We explain this in detail and say: What they use as evidence is either an intellectual argument or an auditory argument. As for rationalities: it is known that the rational arguments that indicate the corruption of what Christians say are more evident than what they use as evidence for the validity of their religion. And whoever among them or the Jews uses a rational argument for violating any part of his religion has answers: one of them is to explain that this It is related to other prophets, for they brought that or something greater than it.

So no one should slander Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - with a rational argument unless that was done by the first path in other prophets. As we explained in the response to the Rafidah, no one should criticize the three caliphs: Abu Bakr, Omar, and Othman, unless he can criticize something like this. This is greater than that in Ali, so it is impossible for Ali to be free from the accusations of his Imamate, unless the three are more safe than him from what is blamed on him. Their leadership.

It is impossible for Moses, Jesus, and David to be innocent of anything that slanders their prophecy, unless Muhammad is innocent of anything that slanders his prophecy. This is as if someone were to use as evidence what is in the Qur’an that proves the attributes, and he would be told: In the Torah and other books of the prophets, such as That is greater, and if he uses the revelation of the resemblances as evidence, he is told: In the previous books there is greater resemblance than in the Qur’an. Did the Christians go astray except by following the ambiguous words of the prophets and abandoning the decisive ones? .

The second: To make clear that this argument is not suitable to be used to oppose what the prophets brought. Just as if some people began to challenge any of the laws based on their opinion, it would become clear to them that what has been proven from the prophets cannot be contradicted by opinion or Measurement.

Third: To show the falsity of that rational argument. If it is based on information, explain its corruption, as we have explained about that in the book “Preventing the Conflict of Reason and Sharia” and mentioned Everything that is used as evidence in contradiction to the texts of the prophets from rational matters is false. We mentioned what waste depends on in this regard.

If it is a matter of requests, then it is a matter of commands and prohibitions. Whoever is in his doctrine does not explain the rulings of God and does not say: The goodness and badness of actions are known by reason, and God does not protect them from Either by action or by ruling, rather everything is permissible for him, but he only denies that by hearsay or custom, so this person will be answered with this answer. But general hearts and minds do not accept this.

As for what the public says: We explain what is in his commands of wisdom and benefits, and what is in his prohibitions of harm and harm. We show the superiority of what he brought over what contradicts it, and we even explain the superiority of the laws of the prophets over the policies of other nations. The preponderance of the law of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - over all other laws, and this has been explained in several places.

But if the People of the Book protest against contradicting Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - with an auditory argument, whether it is from his words, or the words of others, Among the prophets, peace be upon them, the answer was in several ways: One of them was that it was said to them: You cannot believe in the prophecy of a prophet from The prophets while disbelieving in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The way in which the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - is confirmed is through something like it and something greater than it.

Rather, we clarify that believing in his prophecy is better than believing in the prophecy of others, and that everything that is used as evidence of the prophecy of a prophet is Muhammad. Is more deserving of the kind of evidence than any other, and that which contradicts the prophecy of a prophet, so the answer from Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - is more deserving of the answer than the answer. From others.

It is presented in what indicates prophecy, and in what it responds to opposition, and this is more complete in that. It is forbidden, with knowledge or justice, to believe in the prophecy of others while disbelieving in his prophecy, just as it is forbidden with knowledge and justice in all Two people, one of them more perfect than the other in an art, are acknowledged to know that art to the virtuous rather than the virtuous. And we say: with knowledge and justice; Because the oppressor prefers the preferred, even though he knows that it is preferable, and the ignorant person may know the preferred, but not the virtuous.

For many people know the virtue of those they follow: either in knowledge or worship, but they do not know the news of anything other than that, until there are people who They venerate some followers rather than the follower, who is better than the follower, while others they do not know. These people have no knowledge; That is why you find many of these people preferring the preferred; Due to his lack of knowledge of the news of the virtuous, and this is found in all types, even in cities, a person prefers a city that he knows over a city that is He is more complete than her because he does not know her.

Judging between two things by similarity or difference requires knowing each of them and knowing the characteristics through which similarity occurs. Differentiation is like someone who wants to know that Al-Bukhari is more knowledgeable than Muslim, and his book is more correct, or that Sibawayh is more knowledgeable than Al-Akhfash, and so on. That.
And God has favored some of the prophets over others, as God Almighty said: {And We have favored some of the prophets over others} [Al-Isra: 55]..
And God Almighty said: And those messengers We preferred, some of them over others.

The discussion is about two things: One of them: about the fact that the virtuous deserves that status over the virtuous, and this is the ultimate level of ignorance and injustice. Like the saying of the Rafidites who say: Ali was a knowledgeable and just imam, and the three were not like that.

And likewise the Jews and Christians who say: Moses was a messenger, and Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was not like that, for this is in The utmost ignorance and injustice. Unlike those who acknowledge that both deserve status, but prefer the preferred, this is less ignorant and unjust.

It is known that messengers differ, sometimes about the books revealed to them, sometimes about the signs and miracles that indicate their truthfulness, and sometimes about The laws and what they brought of knowledge and work, and sometimes to their nations.

So whoever has knowledge and justice; He looks at the Qur’an and other books such as the Torah and the Bible, or at the miracles of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and the miracles of others. Or in his law and the law of others, or in his nation and the nation of others, he was found to have an advantage over others that is not hidden except from someone who is excessive in Ignorance or injustice.
With this, how can it be said: He is a liar and slanderer, and someone other than him is the true prophet? ! ..

Yes, many of the People of the Book did not know of his information that would explain this to them, just as many of the Shiites did not know of his information. There is nothing that clarifies to them the virtue of Ali, may God be pleased with him, for the three of them. These people are in ignorance, and seeking knowledge is obligatory upon them, especially the command of Prophecy. Considering the matter of the one who said: “Indeed, I am the Messenger of God to you” [Al-A’raf: 158].

prior to everything; Since believing in this is necessary for the end of happiness, and disbelieving in it is necessary for the end of misery, then it is through the Messenger that the difference between the happy people occurs. And the wretched, and between truth and falsehood, guidance and error, and the difference between the friends of God and His enemies.

This also follows the rational path in analogy and consideration, by considering the condition of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and his book and law. And his nation is in the condition of someone else, his book, and his law, and it will be seen whether they are similar or different, and which of them is better, and if it becomes clear that his condition It would be better if you believed him first, and prevented someone else from being truthful while he was a liar.

Rather, if they were similar, then he must be truthful. Likewise, if they were close, and something else is better, for the prophetic liar does not match. The truthful one, but there is such a discrepancy between them that is not hidden except to the blind people.

Likewise, We follow this path among the Prophets - peace be upon them - in general, and among their nations, so that the news of those who passed by will be known. The prophets and their nations. And the effects of these and those will be seen, as God Almighty said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and had hearts with which they reason, or ears with which they hear? For it is not the eyes that are blinded, but the hearts within the breasts that are blinded.” [Al-Hajj: 46].

And God Almighty said: {Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them? And the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who feared. Will they not? Do you understand - even when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been lied to, Our help would come to them, so we would save whomever We wished, and Our punishment would not be averted from the people. Criminals - Indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated hadith, but the truth of what is before it and the detailing of everything is guidance. And a mercy for a people who believe.” [Joseph: 109-111].
And He - the Almighty - said when He mentioned the family of Pharaoh.:.
{And We have followed them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the rejected} [Al-Qasas: 42].

And likewise God Almighty said - about Aad: {And they will be followed in this world with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Aad has disbelieved in their Lord. A people of Hud} [Hud: 60].
And He - the Almighty - said about the people of Shuaib: “Except as far away from Madinah as Thamud was far away” [Hud: 95].
And when the prophets - peace be upon them - are mentioned, He - the Most High - says: {And We left upon him among the others a peace upon Noah among the worlds} [Al-Saffat: 78].
{Peace be upon Abraham} [Al-Saffat: 109].
{Peace be upon Moses and Aaron} [Al-Saffat: 120]..
{Peace be upon the family of Yasin} [Al-Saffat: 130].
And He - the Almighty - said: {And We made for them a tongue of truth exalted} [Maryam: 50].

There are many things like this in the Qur’an. It mentions the condition of the prophets and their followers, the honor that befell them, and what befell the infidels. They are subjected to shame and torment, which clearly shows the good condition of these people and the ugliness of the condition of these people.

What explains this is that those who consider the condition of people of religion, including Muslims, Jews, Christians, and the condition of others, regarding beneficial sciences And good deeds, it became clear to him that the condition of the people of religion is infinitely more perfect. And if one considers the scientific and practical wisdom of non-religious people, such as the wisdom of India, Greece, and the Arabs of pre-Islamic times, And the horse.

And others, it was found that some of them lacked the scientific and practical wisdom of the religious people, so it is impossible for them to be Greek scholars. The Indians and their like are upon truth and guidance, and the scholars of the Muslims, Jews, and Christians are upon falsehood and misguidance. Likewise, it is impossible for the nation to have useful knowledge and righteous deeds, while the people of religious sects are not like that.

In summary: There is no beneficial knowledge and good deeds found among people other than the people of religion, including scientific and practical wisdom, except for the people of Religions are more perfect, and there is no evil among the people of that religion except that it is greater in others.

These Greek philosophers, who were known to many people as wisdom, and whose wisdom was like the wisdom of other nations, were of two types: Innate and practical; And the process in morals, the policy of the home, the policy of cities, and everyone who contemplated what the Jews and Christians had after the abrogation. Changing the policy of morals, home, and cities found him many times better than those of them.
For those are the mainstay of their affairs: speaking about the lustful powers of the soul.

And anger, and the power of knowledge and justice, are like matters of the kind of etiquette of wise people, who do not have knowledge of God, His angels, and His books. And His Messengers, and from worshiping Him alone, without any partner, there is anything of value to Him, and what they have of natural sciences and calculations is not of any benefit. After death, unless it is used for what is beneficial after death. What they have of divine knowledge is very little, although it contains many errors.

Everything they have of useful knowledge and righteous deeds is part of what the prophets - peace be upon them - brought, so it cannot be. These so-called wise men and their followers are right in belief, truthful in words, and good in deeds, as is the goal. What they want. The prophets and their followers are not like that.

Consider this in terms of those who are known from the elite of these people and their common people, and especially these people and their common people, even if there is a discrepancy between them among the people of Paradise and the people of Hell, so consideration in such a matter is what was brought about in the revelation.
He - the Almighty - said: {Allah is better. Do they not associate partners?} [An-Naml: 59].
What is meant is that by consideration, rational measurement, and balancing, the thing is weighed with its equivalent, and the measurement of repulsion and the measurement of The opposite.

It becomes clear to everyone who reflects on this that the people of that religion are more deserving of truth, honesty, and goodness than others, even if they have wisdom. What suits their circumstances. Their wise men are better than their common people, and they are better than the disbelievers in the Messengers, in whom there is no good at all. This is what the followers of the Prophet have benefited from. The prophets are among them, so this is one of the evidences of their prophecy and signs of their message, inferring the effect on the effect and the effect on His reason.

Likewise, whoever contemplates the condition of the Muslims, and the condition of the Jews and Christians, the preponderance of the condition of the Muslims will become clear to him, so this is one of the indications of prophecy. Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and the signs of his message.

We have mentioned elsewhere in this place that prophecy is taught in many ways, and we have mentioned multiple ways of knowing the truthful and prophetic prophet. The liar, other than the path of miracles. Whenever people’s need to know something becomes stronger, God facilitates its causes just as He facilitates what their need for it was in their bodies. More severe, since their need for breath and air was greater than for water, it was given to everyone at all times, and since it was Their need for water was greater than their need for food. The presence of water was greater.

Likewise, since their need to know the Creator was greater, His signs and evidence of his lordship, his ability, his knowledge, and his will were His wisdom is greater than any other wisdom, and since their need to know the truthfulness of the messengers after that was greater than their need for anything else, he established God - Glory be to Him - is among the signs of their truthfulness and evidence of their prophecy and the good condition of those who follow them, his happiness and salvation, and an explanation of what will happen to him. Of useful knowledge and good deeds, and the ugliness of the condition of those who oppose them, their misery, ignorance and injustice - is apparent to those who reflect on that.
{And whoever Allah does not make for him light, he has no light} [An-Nour: 40].

This is what we mentioned about considering a thing by its counterparts, similarities, and similarities, and considering it by its opposites and dissimilarities, until it is known in Among those who are similar, which of them is more perfect and better, and among those who are different, which of them is more deserving of truth and guidance, and justice exists in all matters. His knowledge and practice, such as the science of medicine, arithmetic, jurisprudence, and other things, make it impossible - with knowledge and justice - to be said: Galen was a doctor. Hippocrates was not a doctor, or it could be said: Tamimitus was a philosopher, and Aristotle was not a philosopher, or it could be said:
Al-Akhfash was a grammarian and Sibawayh was not a grammarian, or it could be said: Zufar, Al-Hasan bin Ziyad, and Muhammad bin Al-Hasan were jurists, and Abu Hanifa was not a jurist, or Ashhab
Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb were jurists, and Malik was not a jurist, or that al-Muzani, al-Buwayti, and Harmala were jurists, and al-Shafi’i He was not a jurist, and Abu Dawud and Ibrahim Al-Harbi.

Abu Bakr al-Athram were jurists, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal was not a jurist, or Ali was a just imam, and Abu Bakr and Omar were not. Either they were just imams, or that Nur al-Din al-Shaheed was just, and Omar bin Abdul Aziz was not just, or that Koshyar knew The body, and Ptolemy did not know the body, or that al-Nabigha al-Ja’di was a poet, and al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani was not a poet, or To be said:

The moon is enlightened, but the sun is not enlightened, or that Mercury is a piercing star, and Saturn is not a piercing star, or that a Muslim was a scientist. By hadith, and Al-Bukhari was not like that, or his book is more authentic than Al-Bukhari’s book. And other things that are too long to enumerate.

chapters.title: Detailing their requirement for the validity of prophecy to be preached to the prophets and to respond to them
paragraphs: [Chapter: Their condition for the validity of prophecy is that the prophets be given good tidings about it and respond to them.]

Chapter: The Christians have a famous question among them, which is that there are those among them who say: Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - was not heralded by the prophecies. In contrast to Christ, for he was heralded by prophecies. They claimed that whoever has not been heralded is not a prophet. This question is presented in two ways: one of them: He is not a prophet until you preach the good news to him.

The second: That the one about whom she preached is better or more complete than the one about whom she did not preach, or that this is a path by which the prophecy of Christ is known, he was singled out for him.

And you said: “There is no path by which the prophecy of a prophet is proven except that Muhammad’s prophecy is proven by a path similar to that and better.” So as for this The second one deserves an answer, and as for the first, we will answer them as well. But is it necessary to answer it? There are two opinions based on the principle, which is: Is it a condition for abrogation to notify the abrogated? Muslim commentators have two opinions about it:
One of them: If he enacts a ruling that he wants to abrogate, then he must make those being addressed feel that he will abrogate it; Lest they think it will last, and that would be their ignorance.
The second is not a condition.
Also, whoever was sent after Moses, should he be given good tidings? There are two sayings about it.

In any case, there is no doubt among Muslim scholars that Christ - peace be upon him - gave good tidings of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace - as God Almighty said: {And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, “O Children of Israel, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings of a Messenger whose name will come after me.” Ahmad} [As-Saff: 6].

And God Almighty said: {Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. He commands them He enjoins what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the evil, and relieves them of their burden and the shackles that It was upon them} [Al-A’raf: 157].

And God Almighty said: {Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are harsh against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. You will see them bowing down and prostrating, seeking bounty from God. And contentment. He marked them on their faces as a result of prostration. That is their likeness in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel, like a seed that has brought forth its shoots and strengthened it. So he became violent and established himself on his stems, overwhelming the farmers, thereby angering the disbelievers.} [Al-Fath: 29].
And He - the Almighty - said: {Those to whom We have given the Book know it as they know their own children} [Al-Baqarah: 146].
In two places in the Qur’an: One of them is about monotheism and the Qur’an, and the other is about the Qiblah, the Qur’an, and Muhammad.

So he said in the first place: {Say: “Which thing is greater than witness?” Say: “Allah is Witness between me and you. And this Qur’an has been revealed to me that I may warn you therewith and whomever it reaches.” Do you bear witness that with God there are other gods? Say, “I do not bear witness.” Say, “Indeed, He is only one God, and I am disassociated from what you associate with Him.” - Those to whom We have given They know the Scripture as they know their own children; they have lost their souls, so they do not believe.} [Al-An'am: 19-20]...
This is in Surat Al-An'am, which is Meccan.
He said in Surah Al-Baqarah - which is a Medinan verse -:

{We may see the turning of your face in the sky, so We will certainly turn you to a qiblah that pleases you. So turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, so turn away. Your faces are on the side of it. Indeed, those who were given the Book know that it is the truth from their Lord, and God is not unaware of what they do - and if you were to go to those who were given The Scripture says, “They will not follow your qiblah, nor will you follow their qiblah, nor will some of them follow the qiblah of one another, even if you follow their desires.” After the knowledge that has come to you, then you are indeed among the wrongdoers - those to whom We have given the Scripture recognize it as they recognize their own children, and indeed a party of them They conceal the truth while they know - the truth is from your Lord, so do not be of those who doubt.} [Al-Baqarah:

And God Almighty said: {And previously they used to seek victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers} [Al-Baqarah: 89] .

And He Almighty said: {Is it other than Allah that I seek a judge? When He is the One who has sent down to you the Book in detail, and those to whom We have given the Book know that it was sent down from Your Lord is in truth, so do not be of those who doubt.” [Al-An’am: 114].
And He - the Almighty - said: {Have there not been a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel should not have known?} [Al-Shu’ara’: 197].
And He Almighty said: {Say, “Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you and whoever has knowledge of the Scripture” [Al-Ra’ad: 43].
And He Almighty said: {And when they hear what was sent down to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized} [Al-Maeda: 83].

And He Almighty said: {Indeed, those who were given knowledge before him, when it is recited to them, bow down to their chins in prostration and say, Glory be to our Lord, if it is a promise. Our Lord, indeed, will be fulfilled - and they bow down to their chins, weeping, and their humility increases.} [Al-Isra: 107-109].

And God Almighty said: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it. And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. It is the truth from our Lord. We were Muslims before him - those will be given their reward twice because they were patient, and they avert evil with good, and spend out of what We have provided them.} [Al-Qasas: 52 - 54].
And God Almighty said: {Then if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who read the Book before you} [Yunus: 94]..

If this is the case, then it is said: It is known by the agreement of the people of religion, that it is not a condition of the prophecy of every prophet that he be heralded by those before him; Since prophecy is proven without that, especially Noah, Abraham, and others, it is not known that he was given good tidings about them before them, and likewise in general. The prophets who arose among the children of Israel did not bring any glad tidings; Because they were not sent with an abrogated law, like David, Isaiah, and others.

This may only be said of someone who abrogated the law of those before him, just as Christ came by abrogating some of the provisions of the Torah, and so did Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. May God bless him and grant him peace. In such cases, the disputing Muslim scholars and others dispute: Is it required that he be informed of this before abrogation? On two sayings.

Then the Muslims will say: The law of the Torah and the Gospel was not legislated as an absolute law, but rather as a restricted law until the coming of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace. And peace be upon him - This is like a temporary ruling for a purpose and it is not known when it will take place, as God Almighty says: {So pardon and forgive until God brings about His command} [Al-Baqarah: 109]
And God Almighty says: {So detain them in the houses until death takes them or God makes for them a way} [An-Nisa: 15].
Such things are permissible according to the consensus of the people of religion.

Is this called copying? There are two opinions about it: It was said: It is not called abrogation, like the known purpose, as God Almighty says: {And eat and drink until the white thread becomes clear to you. From the black thread of dawn, then complete the fast until night} [Al-Baqarah: 187].
The removal of the obligation of fasting with the coming of night is not called abrogation, according to people’s agreement.

It was said: An unknown goal is like information. It was said: Rather, this is called abrogation. But this abrogation is permissible with the agreement of the Jewish sects and others, and based on this, the prophethood of Christ and Muhammad is proven - may God’s prayers And His peace be upon them - do not rely on the disputed permissibility of copying, for that is only an absolute ruling. The previous laws were not enacted at all.

Whether it is said: Notifying the abrogator is obligatory, or it is said: It is not obligatory, according to both opinions, the people of the first Islamic law have felt that It will be copied. Moses, Christ, and other prophets also preached Muhammad, and if This is the reality. The prophecy of Christ and Muhammad - may God bless them and grant them peace - does not depend on proving the disputed abrogation.

Then we say that knowledge of the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and the prophecy of Christ does not depend on knowledge that those before them He preached about them, but there are many ways of knowing prophecy. If his prophecy is known in one of the ways, then his prophecy is confirmed by the one who knew that, even if he did not know that those before him had given him good tidings. But it is said:

If the obligation or reality is that it is necessary to inform those before him of his coming and that notification of the abrogation of the law of those before him It is obligatory or a reality. This has become a condition of prophecy, and whoever knows his prophecy knows that this has happened, even if it was not conveyed to him.

If the opponent says: Not informing those before him about it discredits his prophecy, and if it is assumed that he did not inform those before him about it, then Informing is a condition of prophecy. That was slander - it was said: The answer here is in two ways:.

One of them is to say: If his prophecy is known because of the signs of prophecy that he rose upon it; Either the preaching of those before him was necessary or necessary for his prophecy, or it was not necessary.

If it was not necessary, then it would not have occurred, and if it was necessary, it would be known that it occurred, and if that was the case, it would not have been conveyed to us, since it is not everything she said. We knew it from the previous prophets and it has come down to us, but not everything that Christ and the prophets before him told about has come down to us, and this is one of It is taught by necessity.

If it were assumed that this is not in the existing books, it does not follow that Christ and those before him did not mention him. Rather, it is possible that they mentioned him and what It was transferred, and it may have been in books other than these, or it may have been in versions other than these, so it was removed from some of them, and this one was abrogated. Of what was removed from it, and those copies in which it exists are other than this one, so all of this is usually possible, but it is not possible to say with certainty that it is denied.

If it were assumed that it is not in these books that exist today in the hands of the People of the Book, it would not be certain that the prophets did not give good tidings of it. If the Jews cannot be certain that Christ was not preached by the prophets, and the People of the Book cannot be certain that Muhammad was not given good tidings by the prophets. They had no knowledge of the opposite. Rather, it was only a suspicion on the part of one of them because it was a request. He did not find it.

The evidence of the prophecy of Christ and Muhammad is conclusive and certain, and it cannot be discredited with suspicion. Suspicion does not support certainty, especially with the many narrations informing that Muhammad’s name was written explicitly, as is narrated on the authority of The Prophets, as in Sahih Al-Bukhari, where it was said to Abdullah bin Amr: “Tell us some of the characteristics of the Messenger of God in the Torah,” and he said:

It is described in the Torah with some description in the Qur’an: “O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good news and a warner and a protector for the unlettered. You are My servant and My Messenger. I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. You are not rude, harsh, or noisy in the markets, and you do not repay evil with evil, but you reward With good and bad, and pardon and forgive, and I will not seize him until I establish the religion with him.
Waves, so he opened blind eyes, deaf ears, and uncircumcised hearts, by saying there is no god but Allah.

The words of the Torah, the Gospel, the Qur’an, and the Psalms may mean the specific books, or they may mean the type, so the Qur’an means the Psalms. And others, as in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace -: “The Qur’an was made easy for David, and it was between the time when his animal was saddled that... He rides it and recites the Qur’an. “And what is meant by it is the Qur’an, which is the Psalms. What is meant by it is not the Qur’an which was not revealed except to Muhammad.
Likewise, what was mentioned in the description of the nation of Muhammad: “Their bibles in their breasts.” So he called the books they read - which are the Qur’an - bibles.

Likewise in the Torah: “Indeed, I will raise up for the children of Israel a prophet from among their brothers. I will send down to him a Torah like the Torah of Moses.” So he called the second book. Torah.

His saying: “Inform me of the description of the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - in the Torah” may mean all of the same books mentioned above, and all of them. It is called the Torah, and this is the case in some of it.

What is meant by this may be the specific Torah. Based on this, this is in a copy from which none of these copies were abrogated, as the existing copies This is not the case in the Torah that we have learned.
But this, according to them, is in the prophecy of Isaiah, in which he said:

“My servant, in whom my soul is well pleased, I will send down my revelation to him, and he will show my justice among the nations and give them commandments. He will not laugh, nor will his voice be heard in markets, opens blind eyes and deaf ears, revives uncircumcised hearts, and what I give I do not give to anyone, he praises God with a new praise that comes from to the ends of the earth, and the wilderness and its inhabitants will rejoice, glorifying God with every honor and glorifying Him on every hill. He will not weaken, nor be defeated, nor incline. To his passion, he is displeasing and does not humiliate the righteous who are like a weak reed, but rather strengthens the righteous, and he is the pillar of the humble, and he is the light of God who It is not extinguished.
The trace of his authority is on his shoulders.”
These are characteristics that apply to Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and his nation, and they are because of the glad tidings of the prophets who preceded him.

The word Torah has been known to mean the type of books that the People of the Book acknowledge, so this includes the Psalms and the prophecy of Isaiah. And all other prophecies other than the Gospel.
If what is meant by the word “Torah and Gospel” in the Qur’an is this meaning; There is no doubt that the mention of the Prophet in the Torah is many and numerous.

The second way of answering: To show that the prophets before him preached about it. This is independent evidence of his prophecy and a great sign of his message, and this - also - indicates the prophecy of that prophet when he informed With news from the unseen along with the claim of prophethood, and indicates the prophecy of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - to inform those whose prophethood is proven By his prophecy. This is if the news is found from someone whose prophecy we do not know, and he is not mentioned in our book.

As for those whose prophecy was proven in other ways, such as Moses and Christ, this is one of the things in which the evidence of a single meaning is apparent, and it is - also - It implies that everything by which someone else’s prophecy is proven, his own prophecy is also proven, and it is a second answer to those who make that a necessary condition. For his prophecy.

chapters.title: Separating the methods of knowledge of the prophets’ good news of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him
paragraphs: [Chapter: Methods of knowledge based on the prophets’ good news of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him]
A chapter, then the knowledge that the prophets before him gave good tidings about it is known in many ways.:.
One of them: what is mentioned in the books that exist today in the hands of the People of the Book.

Second: Informing those who came across these books and other books of the People of the Book - from those who converted to Islam and those who did not - about what they found of mentioning it. In it.

This is like what was narrated on the authority of the Ansar, that their neighbors from the People of the Book used to inform of his being sent, and that he was the Messenger of God, and that It exists with them, and this was one of the greatest things he called the Ansar to believe in when he called them to Islam, until the Ansar believed in it. They pledged allegiance to him without fear or desire.
For this reason it was said: The city was conquered by the Qur’an, not by the sword as others were conquered.

And just as the Christians repeatedly reported its presence in their books, such as the reports of Heraclius, the king of the Romans, and Al-Muqawqis, the king of Egypt, the companion of Alexandria and Negus, king of Abyssinia, and those who came to him in Mecca, and God mentioned that in the Qur’an in what He said about the Jews.:.
{And previously they used to seek victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it} [Al-Baqarah: 89].

He said about the Christians: {And when they hear what was revealed to the Messenger, you will see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They will say, “Our Lord, we believe.” So We are recorded with the witnesses} [Al-Maeda: 83].
And His saying: {Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it, and when it is recited to them, they say, “We believe in it. It is the truth from our Lord” [Al-Qasas: 52].

Ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah or on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Jews were They attacked the Aws and Khazraj with the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - before he was sent. When God sent him from among the Arabs, they disbelieved in him. And they denied what they were saying about it.” Then Muadh bin Jabal, Bishr bin Al-Baraa bin Ma’rur, and Dawud bin Salamah said:

“O Jews, fear God and submit to Islam, for you used to incline to us by means of Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - and we are people of polytheism.” And you tell us that he has been sent and describe him with his description.” Salam bin Mishkam, the brother of Banu al-Nadir, said, “Nothing has come to us that we know of, and what it is.” “What we used to mention to you.”
Then God Almighty revealed: {But when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it, so the curse of God is upon the disbelievers} [Al-Baqarah: 89].

Abu Al-Aliya and others said: “Whenever they - meaning the Jews - sought victory through Muhammad against the Arab polytheists, they would say: O God, send this prophet which we find written with us, until We torture the polytheists and kill them.” Then when God sent Muhammad and they saw that he was from others, they disbelieved in him out of envy For the Arabs, and they know that he is the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - so God revealed these verses.
{But when what they recognized came to them, they disbelieved in it} [Al-Baqarah: 89].

Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada al-Ansari, then al-Dhufri, on the authority of men from his people who said: “And from what he called us to Islam - with the mercy and guidance of God - we used to hear from Jewish men. We were polytheists, adherents of idols, and they were People of the Book. They have knowledge that we do not have, and there was still evil between us and them, so when we got from them some of what they disliked, they would say to us:

The time has approached when a prophet will be sent. Now we will follow him and kill you with him like Aad and Iram. We often heard that from them. When he was sent God is His Messenger - may God bless him and grant him peace - a messenger from God. We responded when he called us to God, and we knew what they were threatening us with. So We hastened to it, and we believed in it, but they disbelieved in it, so among us and among them these verses were revealed.
That in the cow.:.

{And when there came to them a book from Allah, confirming what they have. And previously they were seeking victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them what they recognized, they disbelieved in it. So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers} [Al-Baqarah: 89].

He said: Ibn Ishaq: “Salih bin Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman bin Awf narrated to us, Yahya bin Abdullah bin Abdullah narrated to us Al-Rahman bin Asaad bin Zurarah Al-Ansari, he said: Whoever of the men of my people I wanted told me on the authority of Hassan bin Thabit Al-Ansari, he said: By God, I am a young boy, seven or eight years old, who understands all that I have heard. I heard a Jew saying about the sheep of Yathrib, shouting: “O community of Jews.” When they gathered around him, they said: “What is the matter with you?” He said: “The star of Ahmad has risen tonight.”

Abu Zar’ah narrated, with an authentic chain of transmission, on the authority of Usama bin Zaid, on the authority of his father Zaid bin Haritha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out Then the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - came on a hot day in Mecca, until we were at the top of the valley. Zayd bin Amr bin Nufayl met him, and the Messenger of God said to him: “O son of Amr, what is wrong with me when I see your people hang you up?” ".

He said: “By God, this is not due to my dissatisfaction with them, but I see them as being astray.” So I went out seeking this religion, so I came to The rabbis of Yathrib, and I found them worshiping God and associating partners with Him, so I said: This is not the religion I seek. So I went out to go to the rabbis of Khaybar, and I found them worshiping God and associating partners with Him. I said: This is not the religion I seek. Then the rabbi said to me: From the rabbis of the Levant: “You are asking about a religion that we do not know of anyone who worships God except an old man on the island.” So I went out and went to him and told him what I had gone out for, and he said:
“Indeed, everyone you see is in error, so who are you?” I said: “I am from the people of the House of God, and from the people of thorns and thorns.”

He said: “Indeed, a prophet has risen in your country - or: a foreigner - whose star has risen, so go back and believe him, follow him, and believe in him. I returned but did not feel anything. After that, he said: “Then the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - let his camel down, so we brought the meal to it.” Zaid said: “I do not eat anything slaughtered for anyone other than God.” So they separated, and the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - came and went around the house. Zaid said: I was with him, and there were two idols of copper called:
(Isaf) and (Na’ilah) facing the Kaaba, people wipe them when they circumambulate. The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: “Do not touch them or Wipe with them.”

Zaid said: So I said to myself - while we had gone around - to touch them until I saw what he was saying, so I touched them, and the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - said - Did you not forbid him? “By the one who honored him, I did not touch them until God sent down the Book to him.”
“Zayd bin Amr bin Nufayl died before Islam. Then the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - said: “He will send a nation alone.”
Al-Bukhari narrated the hadith of the departure of Zaid bin Amr that is close to this wording.

And he said: Ibn Ishaq: Saleh bin Ibrahim bin Abdul Rahman bin Awf told us, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid, on the authority of Salama bin Salama bin And Qash, he said: There was a Jew among our people, so he went out to the club of his people, Banu Abd al-Ashhal, one morning, and mentioned the resurrection and the resurrection. And Paradise and Hell and the Reckoning and the Balance, and he said that to the people of an idol, who do not see that a resurrection exists after death, and that was before a resurrection. Messenger of God, and they said: “Woe to you, O so-and-so - or: Woe to you - and this is happening, that people are sent after their death to an abode in which there is Paradise and Hell.” They will be rewarded for their deeds,” he said:

“Yes, and by the one by which he swears, I wish that my share of that fire was that you would light the largest oven in your house, and you would warm it, and then you would throw me into it, then You are putting rain on me and I will escape from that fire tomorrow. It was said: O so-and-so, what is the sign of that? He said: “A prophet will be sent from this country.” He pointed to Mecca and Yemen with his hand. They said: “When will you see him?” He looked over and saw me

I was lying in the courtyard of my family’s door and I was talking to the people. He said: “If this boy spends his life, he will realize it.” Then the night passed. And the day until God sent His Messenger, and he was alive among them, so we believed in him and believed him, but he disbelieved in him out of transgression and envy, so we said to him: Oh Were you not the one who said what you said and told us? He said: It is not.

On the authority of Anas bin Malik - may God be pleased with him - “A Jewish boy was serving the Prophet, and he fell ill, so the Messenger of God came to visit him, and he found his father At his head, he was reading the Torah, and the Messenger of God said to him: O Jew, I adjure you by God, who sent down the Torah to Moses, do you find in the Torah My characteristic and my way out? He said: No. The boy said: “Yes, by God, O Messenger of God. We find in the Torah your description and your exit, and I bear witness that there is no god but God.” And that you are the Messenger of God, so he said:

The Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - set this man at his head, and befriend your brother.” Narrated by Al-Bayhaqi with an authentic chain of transmission. And he said: Ibn Ishaq: Asim bin Omar bin Qatada told me, on the authority of a sheikh from Banu Qurayzah, who said: Do you know what Usayd’s conversion to Islam was? And my son's alopecia

Sa’iyyah, and Asad bin Ubaid, a group of people from Hadal, who were not from Banu Qurayzah and Banu An-Nadir. They were above that, so I said: No. He said: For it is A Jewish man from the Levant, called Ibn al-Hiban, came to us and stayed with us. By God, we have never seen a man who did not pray the five prayers well. From him, he came to us years before the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - was sent, and when we became droughty and the rain became scarce, we would say: O son of Al-Hibban, “Go out and draw water for us.” He said: “No, by God, until you give alms before your exit,” and we say: “How much?”
Then he would say: A saa of dates or a handful of barley, so we would take him out. Then he would go out to the outside of our neighborhood and we would be with him.

So we draw water, and by God, he will not rise from his seat until the reefs pass by. He did that more than once, not twice, or three times, then death approached him and they gathered around him, and he said: O community of Jews, what do you think has taken me out of From the land of wine and yeast to the land of misery and hunger? They said: You know best. He said:

“For he brought me out, expecting the emergence of a prophet whose time had been lost. This is the land of his migration, so follow him and do not rush to him when he emerges. O community of Jews, he will be sent to shed blood, and to captivate the children and women of those who oppose him, and that will not prevent you from him.” Then he died, and when It was the night that Qurayzah was conquered, and those three young men - and they were young men - said: O community of Jews, by God, it is he who Ibn Al-Hayban mentioned to you, and they said: What is the matter with him? They said:
“Yes, by God, that is his characteristic.” Then they descended, converted to Islam, and left their property and children behind.
And their families. Ibn Ishaq said: When the fort was opened, it was returned to them.

And in the two Sahih books there is a hadith of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Abu Sufyan bin Harb, when he told him on the authority of Heraclius - and his hadith was presented at the beginning of the book - He mentioned in it that when Heraclius asked him about the characteristics of the Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - he said: If what you say is true, that he is a prophet, then I was I know that he is outside, and I did not think that he was one of you, and if I had known that I would be sincere to him, I would have loved to meet him, and if I had been with him, I would have washed away his sins. His feet.
Al-Bukhari added in his hadith, and Ibn al-Natour said: Heraclius was.

A mourner looked at the stars, and he looked and said: The king of circumcision has appeared. Who among this nation will circumcise? He said: Circumcise the Jews, and do not care about them, but send to the Jews in your kingdom and they will kill them. Then he found an Arab and said: Look, is he circumcised? They looked and saw that he was circumcised. He asked him about the Arabs, and he said: They are circumcised. And he said in it:

There was a friend of his in Rome, Heraclius was his equal in knowledge, so he sent for him, and he went to Homs, and he did not leave Homs until a letter came to him from Its owner agrees with his opinion about the emergence of the Prophet - may God bless him and grant him peace - and that he is a prophet.

Likewise, Al-Najashi, king of Abyssinia, when the companions migrated to him, when the polytheists harmed them and feared that they would tempt them from their religion, and they read The Qur’an is upon him. He said: Then he took a stick between his two fingers and said: Except for Jesus, son of Mary, I did not say this stick. Then his two fingers quarreled, and he said: And if you snort. Go, for you are living in my land. It means you are safe. He said this because the Quraysh sent gifts to him and asked him to return these Muslims, and they said: “These have abandoned our religion and gone against us.” “Your religion.”

And in the Sahih, the hadith of Waraqah bin Nawfal, which was narrated by Aisha - may God be pleased with her - regarding the beginning of the revelation, she said: “The first thing with which it began The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - was inspired by a true vision from sleep, and he never saw a vision except that it came like the breaking of dawn, then He loved the solitude, so he used to be alone in the caves of Hira and spend many, many nights in it - which is devotion - until she said - so she brought him Khadija Waraqah bin Nawfal, who had converted to Christianity during pre-Islamic times, and used to write from the Bible whatever God wished to be written, so she said:
Hear from your nephew. The Messenger of God - may God bless him and grant him peace - told him what he saw. Waraqah said: This is the law that God sent down to Musa, I wish I had
