And the Almighty said: {And it is a revelation of the Lord of the worlds - the Faithful Spirit has sent it down - to your heart that you may be among the warners - in a clear Arabic language - and indeed, In the sects of the ancients - was there not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel should not know?} [Al-Shu’ara’: 192-197].
To what he said.

{And what the devils have sent down - and it is not for them, nor are they able - they are cut off from hearing - so do not call upon another god with God, lest you be Of those who are tormented - and warn your closest family - and lower your wing to those of the believers who follow you - but if they disobey you, say, “I am innocent of what you do.” - And put your trust in the Mighty, the Most Merciful - He who sees you when you rise - and your turning among those who prostrate - Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing - Shall I inform you upon whom it was revealed? The devils - descend upon every wicked creature - they slander people, but most of them are liars - and the poets are followed by the deceitful - Have you not seen that they are in every valley? They wander - and they say what they do not do - except those who believe and do righteous deeds and remember God much and are victorious after they have been wronged. And those who have wronged will know to what turn they will turn.} [Al-Shu’ara’:
Then God Almighty said: {And indeed, it is among the hearts of the ancients} [Al-Shu’ara’: 196].
And he said: {Has there not been a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel should have known?} [Al-Shu’ara’: 197].

And the scholars of the Children of Israel know the mention of the sending of Muhammad and the descending of the revelation to him, as God Almighty said: {Which they find written with them in The Torah and the Gospel} [Al-A’raf: 157].
And He said: {And those to whom We have given the Book know that it has been sent down from your Lord in truth, so do not be of those who doubt} [Al-An’am: 114].
And He said: {Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it believe in it} [Al-Qasas: 52].
And he said: {And when it is recited to them, they say, “We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before Him.” [Al-Qasas: 53].
They know the meanings in it that they agree with the sayings of the messengers before him regarding the news and the matter.

For he informed about the oneness of God, His attributes, His throne, His angels, His creation of the heavens and the earth, and other than that in a manner similar to what was reported. The messengers before him. He commanded the monotheism of God and worshiping Him alone, without any partner, and with justice, truthfulness, prayer, and zakat, and forbade polytheism and injustice. And immoral acts, as the messengers before him commanded and prohibited.

The Meccan surahs were revealed according to the common universal principles, which the Messengers agreed upon, and which are indispensable, which is general Islam. God does not accept from any of the ancients or the lasts a religion other than His.

As for the Medinan surahs, they contain this, and they contain what is specific to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the law and the method. The religion of the prophets is one, as is proven in the Sahih on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “We - the prophets - our religion is one.” God Almighty said: {He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, which We have revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, that you should establish the religion. And do not become divided therein} [Al-Shura: 13].

And the Almighty said: {O you messengers, eat of the good things and do righteousness. Indeed, I am All-Knowing of what you do - and this is your nation, a single nation, and I Your Lord, so beware of your duty - so they divided their affairs into divisions between them, each party rejoicing in what they had.} [Al-Mu’minun: 51-53].

And God Almighty said: {So set your face upright toward the religion, upright. It is the nature of God which He created mankind. There is no altering of God’s creation. That is the right religion, but Most people do not know - turn to Him and fear Him and establish prayer and do not be of the polytheists - of those who divided their religion and became sects, each party They rejoice in what they have” [Al-Rum: 30-32].
As for the law and the method, he said about the people of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an: “For each of you We have made a law and a method” [Al-Ma’idah: 48].
And he said:

{And for every nation We have appointed a ritual to mention the name of God over what He has provided for them of livestock. So your God is one God, so to Him do they submit, and give good tidings to them. The hidden ones - those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts fear, and those who are patient over what befalls them, and those who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided them - and the body. We have made it for you among the rituals of God, for you in it is good, so mention the name of God over it in rows, and when it sets in its setting, eat from it and feed the contented. And thus We have made it subservient to you that you may be grateful - its flesh or its blood will not reach God, but piety will attain it from you.} [Al-Hajj:
To his saying: {For every nation We have appointed a ritual which they will follow} [Al-Hajj: 67].
As for the qiblah: He did not make the qiblah what the People of the Book invented, for that is why He said: {And for every destination He is its master} [Al-Baqarah: 148].

He did not say: Indeed, We have appointed a destination for every direction, as He said regarding the rituals, the law, and the method. And the Almighty said: {And they said, “Why should he not bring to us a sign from his Lord? Has there not come to them a clear proof of what is in the earlier pages?” [Ta-ha: 133].

If he brought to them an explanation of what was in the early newspapers - even though they knew that he had not lived with any of the people of the early newspapers, nor benefited from them. Knowledge - This was one of the greatest signs from God.

Just as his informing about matters of the unseen indicates his prophecy, it indicates that prophecy is news from God. This is not what some say. Philosophers like Ibn Sina and his likes say: (It is an overflow of the cosmic soul or active mind that overflowed upon him), and they say: (The soul or active intellect overflows upon him.) The mind is the preserved Tablet, and whoever has his soul connected to it will know what the prophets taught him), and they say: (Prophecy is acquired; Because this is her characteristic), and they say:

(The reason for his knowledge of the unseen is his connection with the cosmic soul), and they claimed that it is the preserved tablet, and that its movement of the cosmic It is the reason for the occurrence of events on earth, so it is aware of what is happening on earth. Because knowledge of the cause necessitates knowledge of the cause. This is based on false premises, the falsehood of which has been widely discussed in other places:
Among them: proving the effective mind.
Among them: their claim that there is no cause for accidents except the movement of the astronomy.
Among them: that its motive is the soul.
Among them: the connection of our souls with that soul.

What is meant - here - is that if this were true, it would only benefit knowledge of the future for which the present movement is the cause. As for what may Hundreds or thousands of years passed, and none of the movements of the sphere - when the Messenger was sent - caused it. Rather, the movement existing in His time is a reason for the future, not the past, and in that case the soul’s movement of the orbit is not a reason for knowledge of these matters, nor is it It is the Preserved Tablet. Rather, the Glorious Qur’an is in a preserved Tablet, and it is in the Mother of the Book, and it is:
{In a hidden book - none shall touch it except the purified} [Al-Waqi’ah: 78-79].
And God Almighty told us that: “The Trustworthy Spirit descended upon him” [Al-Shu’ara’: 193].
And he said in another verse: “Say, ‘It has been sent down by the Holy Spirit from your Lord in truth.’” [An-Nahl: 102].
And he said: In another place: {Say: Whoever is an enemy of Gabriel - indeed, he has sent it down to your heart, God willing} [Al-Baqarah: 97].

And he said: {Indeed, it is the saying of a noble Messenger - one of power with the Possessor of the Throne, secure - obedient and trustworthy - and your companion is not insane - and he saw it on the horizon. The Clear - and it is not upon the Unseen with longing - and it is not the word of an accursed Satan - so where will you go - it is only a reminder to the worlds - to whomsoever He wills Some of you should be upright} [Al-Takwir: 19-28].
And the Almighty said: {God selects messengers from the angels and from people} [Al-Hajj: 75].

So he mentioned that it was the saying of a Messenger whom He had chosen from among the angels. He revealed it to a Messenger whom He had chosen from among mankind, and he said: {It is the saying of a noble Messenger - And it is not the saying of a poet. Little do you believe - nor the saying of a soothsayer. Little do you remember - a revelation from the Lord of the worlds - even if He were to speak against us. Sayings - We would certainly have taken from him by the right hand - then We would have cut off from him the two jaws - so there is not one of you who will withhold from it - and indeed it is a reminder for the righteous - And we know that among you are deniers - and indeed it is a regret for the disbelievers - and indeed it is the truth of certainty - so glorify the name of your Lord Almighty} [Al-Haqqah: 19 - 52].
So he freed both of the Messengers from whatever might be suspected of them.

The angel was tempted to be a devil, and human beings were tempted to be a poet or a priest, and he explained the proof of that and his sign, saying: {And what was revealed... Therein are the devils - and it is not appropriate for them, nor are they able - that they are isolated from hearing.} [Al-Shu’ara’: 210-212].

So it is clear that it is not appropriate for them to use it, but rather they are forbidden from that, and they abstain from that and do not want it to contradict it. Because of their intended purpose, and if they had wanted to, they would have been unable to do so, so they would not have been able to do it. Since they were isolated from hearing it from the highest assembly, and they were only able to come down by what they heard, not by what they did not hear, This is because the one who does the action only does it if he wants it and is able to do it.
So he explained his saying: {And what is appropriate for them} [Al-Shu’ara’: 211].
Because they do not want to download it.
And by His saying: {And they are not able} [Al-Shu’ara’: 211].
Because they are unable to download it.

As for the fact that they do not want to; Because it is not appropriate for them. (And it is appropriate) is the present tense of ghāḥa yughābhu: that is, he requested and wanted. What the agent should not do is what he does not ask for or want, either because he is abstained from doing so, or because he is prohibited from doing so. Satan only wants lies and immorality, he does not want honesty and righteousness.

What the Messenger brought contradicted the intent of the devils to the extreme, and nothing has occurred on earth greater in contradiction to the intent of the devils than sending Muhammad, so the Qur’an was revealed to him, so he prevents the devils from doing what they only want the opposite of, and they - also - are prevented from that in that they do not This is appropriate for them and does not come from them, just as a magician should not be a prophet.

The one who is known for lying and immorality should not - however - be a prophet, nor a judge, nor a witness, nor a mufti; Since lying and immorality contradict the purpose of judgment, testimony, and fatwas, likewise the desire to lie is in the nature of the devils. Immorality contradicts the use of these words, which are extremely honest and just, and do not include a single lie or injustice to anyone.
Then he said: {And they are not able} [Al-Shu’ara’: 211].

For they will be isolated from hearing these words, because of the meteors with which the sky is guarded, as He said - on the authority of the jinn -: {And We touched the sky. Then we found it filled with strong guards and meteors - and we used to sit in it as seats to listen. But whoever listens now will find a meteor watching over him.} [The Jinns: 8 - 9].

We mentioned the frequency of this news, and that the sky was guarded by a guard that people had never seen before, and people saw that with their own eyes. They had witnessed what he told them about shooting meteors, which is used to cast out demons, and they were thus cut off from the hearing of the public. The highest, and what the infidels witnessed - the general intense shooting - with which the well-known custom of shooting meteors was broken, was evidence of a reason. It was contrary to custom, and nothing had happened - at that time - on earth that was not customary except for his claim of the message, so it was not known who descended before him. The speech is upon him as it descends upon him; Since Moses, peace be upon him, the Torah was only revealed to him in writing, and it was not revealed to him in written form, divided and delivered to him.

For protection, so that the sky needs to guard it from overhearing. The Psalms are subordinate to the law of the Torah, and likewise the Gospel is a branch of the Torah. No separate book was sent down except the Torah and the Qur’an, as God Almighty said: {Say, “Bring a book from Allah. It is more guided than the two of them. I will follow it.” If you are truthful} [Al-Qasas: 49].

That is why God, Glory be to Him, often compares the Torah and the Qur’an, as in His saying: {And they did not estimate God with His true value when they said, “What God has revealed to me.” Good tidings of something. Say, “Who sent down the Book which Moses brought as a light and a guidance for the people?” [Al-An’am: 91].
To his saying: {And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming what is before it} [Al-An’am: 92].

And he said: {Is he who is upon clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from him and before him recites it, and the Book of Moses as a guide and a mercy? Those believe in him, and whoever Whoever of the parties disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his appointed time.} [Hud: 17].

Saeed bin Jubayr and others said: “And the parties are all sects.” He said: This is the confirmation of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And the one who My soul is in His hand. No Jew or Christian from this nation has heard of me, nor has anyone believed in me unless he enters Hell,” and he recited this verse: {And whoever of the parties disbelieves in it - the Fire is his abode} [Hud: 17].
And the jinn said: “Indeed, we heard a book that was sent down after Moses” [Al-Ahqaf: 30].
Al-Najashi said - when he heard the Qur’an -: (Indeed, this is what Moses brought to come out of a single niche).

Also, it was known to them that the soothsayers would tell about the demons that were eavesdropping. When they saw that the sky was guarded by a strong guard, other than Usually, they knew that the devils prevented eavesdropping, and the jinn knew that, as mentioned above, and the jinn said: {And We touched the sky and found it It was filled with strong guards and meteors - and we used to sit therein as seats to listen. But whoever listens now will find a meteor waiting for him.} [Al-Jinn: 8-9].

News has circulated that during the mission there was a lot of shooting of meteors, and this is an extraordinary matter, to the point that some people feared that it might be That is because of the destruction of the world, until they looked at whether they shot at the planets in the orbit or shot at meteors? When they saw that it was by meteors, they knew that something had happened. And the jinn were sent seeking the reason for that, until they heard the Qur’an, and they knew that it was for that reason.
This is one of the signs and evidence of prophecy.

Before and after the time of resurrection, the shooting was light, and the sky was not filled with it as it was filled when the Qur’an was revealed, and God Almighty said: {Shall I inform you? Upon whom do the devils descend - upon whom do they descend upon every sinful avatar?
And the wicked liar, and the sinful and immoral person, as He said: {Let us smite the forelock - a lying, sinful forelock} [Al-Alq: 15-16].

He said in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon: “You must be honest, for honesty leads to Paradise, and a man will continue to tell the truth and strive for honesty until he is written down.” There is a truthful one with God, and beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to Hell, and the man continues to lie. And he seeks to lie until he is written before God as a liar.”

The devils descend upon the one who achieves their purpose by descending upon him, and this is appropriate for them in lying and immorality. As for the truthful and righteous person, the intent of the devils will not be achieved through him, for Satan does not seek honesty and righteousness, but rather seeks a lie. And immorality.

And Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is still known by his people as the truthful and trustworthy. Not a single lie has been tried against him. And when the spirit came to him with the revelation, he did not tell a single false statement, neither intentionally nor mistakenly.

And whoever has the devils descend upon him must tell a lie, for the devils give them what they heard, but they do not give them what they heard on the surface. His face, but they lie about it a lot. Most of the devils who descend upon them are liars about what they descend upon them. And the devils, even if they are all liars - not everyone who delivers a hearing lies about what he delivers, but rather one of them may be truthful in what he delivers. And he steals it, but most of them lie, and the one among them who tells the truth once lies many times, and the one upon whom the devils send down sinful ravages.

The difference between the truthful and righteous person to whom the angel comes, and the sinful liar to whom the accursed Satan comes, is a clear difference, known with the slightest knowledge. In the case of the two, and since the soothsayer to whom a devil comes may tell some unseen matters, God Almighty has made it clear that this will happen - even if it is true. In some reports - a liar and an immoral person, and whoever tells a lie should not be suspected of one who neither lies nor is an immoral person, and this is what shows that A prophet can only be righteous and infallible from insisting on a sin.

chapters.title: Detailing the conclusive evidence of the people of Mecca on the truthfulness of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace
paragraphs: [Chapter: The conclusive evidence among the people of Mecca of the truthfulness of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.]

We have mentioned that his people, who were extremely hostile to him, still acknowledged his sincerity, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that they had not tried They lied to him, and even acknowledged that what he was saying was neither poetry nor soothsaying, and that he was not a magician. At the beginning of his reign, they sent to The country where the scholars of the People of the Book ask them about it; Because Mecca did not have that.

In the two Sahih books on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Sufyan bin Harb told him, saying: “I set out for the Levant during the period that was between me and the Messenger of God.” God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: While I was in the Levant, a letter from the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was brought to Heraclius. He said: And it was Dihya al-Kalbi brought him, and sent him to the chief of Busra, and the chief of Busra sent him to Heraclius, and Heraclius said: Is there anyone here? The people of this man who claims to be a prophet? They said: Yes. He said: I called for a group of Quraysh and we entered upon Heraclius, so we sat before him. He said:

Which of you is closer in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet? Abu Sufyan said: So I said, “I am.” So they made me sit in front of him, and they made my friends sit behind me. So he called for his interpreter and said: Tell them: I am asking this about this man who claims to be a prophet, so if he denies me, then they will deny him.

He said: He said: By God! Were it not for fear that a lie would affect me, I would have lied to him. Then he said to his interpreter: Ask him how he ranks among you? He said: I said: He is worthy of reckoning among us. He said: Was there anyone among his fathers who had kings? I said: No. He said: Were you accusing him of lying before he said what he said? I said: No.” He mentioned the rest of the hadith: And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, the hadith of Saad bin Muadh, when he said to Umayyah: They They killed you (meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions), and he was terrified of that, and he said that to his wife, and she said:

By God, Muhammad does not lie. And he said - in another narration -: By God, Muhammad does not lie, and he resolved not to go out for fear of this. He said: By God, I will never leave Mecca. He wanted to stay behind from Badr, until Abu Jahl said to him: When people see that you have left behind, and you are the master of this valley, they will leave behind with you. He said: If you defeat me, I will buy the best camel in Mecca, and his wife reminded him of what Saad had said, so he said: I do not want to
I will be with them only soon.

Likewise, what was mentioned by the people of Al-Maghazi and others: “When Ubayy bin Khalaf heard that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will kill him, Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stabbed him and scratched him, and his companions made him panic and say: It is just a scratch and nothing, so he said: By God, if he had been in harm’s way, he would have killed them. Didn’t he say: “I will kill you.” On the authority of Mujahid: My master Al-Sa’ib ibn Abi Al-Sa’ib said: I was among those who built The House, and that the Quraysh disagreed about the stone when they wanted to place it, to the point that a sword fight almost broke out between them, so he said:
Make among you the first man to enter through the door. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered, and in pre-Islamic times they called him Al-Amin.
They said: O Muhammad, we are satisfied with you.

On the authority of Aqeel bin Abi Talib, he said: “The Quraysh came to Abu Talib and said to him: Your nephew comes to our Kaaba and calls us and listens to us.” Whatever harms us, if you feel that you can stop it from us, then do so. He said: Then he said to me: O Aqeel, seek out your cousin. Abi Talib’s people, so he started walking until he came to Abu Talib, and he said to him: O son of my brother, by God, I do not know if you will be obedient to me, and he has Your people came to me claiming that you come to them in their Kaaba and call them and make them hear something that annoys them. If you decide to stop it, he said:

So he looked up to the sky and said: By God, I am not able to let what I was sent with be for one of you to ignite from this sun. A flame of fire, and Abu Talib said: “By God, he has never lied, so return with righteousness.” It was narrated by Al-Bukhari in his history, and Abu Zar’ah in Al-Dala’il, and Ibn Ishaq narrated it close to this wording, and he said: “So I brought it out from a sturgeon - It is a small house - and he said in it: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, thought that it had appeared to his uncle, and that he had abandoned him and surrendered him, and was weak in Standing with him, he said:
“O uncle, if the sun were placed in my right hand and the moon in my left hand, I would not leave this matter until God or your family makes it easy in seeking it.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Samit, he said: “Abu Dharr said: We came out of our people forgiving, and they were declaring lawful the sacred month, so I went out.” And my brother Unais and our mother, we camped with a maternal uncle of ours, and he honored us and did good to us. His people envied us, and they said: If you depart from your family, Anis disagreed with them, so our uncle came and spoke to us about what was said to him, so I said to him: As for what you did previously, you have disturbed it, and you have no intercourse regarding it. After that, we approached our ram, and we embraced it, and our uncle covered himself with his garment, crying, and we set off until we came down to the presence of Mecca.

Then Anais, a man, left for our bundle and something like it, so we went to the priest, and he gave Anis a choice, so he brought our bundle and something like it. He said: I prayed, my nephew, three years before I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: For whom? He said: For God’s sake. I said: Where did he go? He said: I go where my Lord directs me, and I pray the evening prayer, until at the end of the night I lie down as if I were invisible, until the sun overshadows me, and he said Anis: I have a need in Mecca, please help me. So Unais set off until he came to Mecca and bequeathed to me, then he came and I said: What have you done? He said:

I met a man in Mecca who follows your religion, claiming that God sent him. I said: What do the people say? He said: They say: a poet, a priest, a magician. Anis was one of the poets. Anis said: I heard what the priests said, but it is not what they say, and I put what he said to the poets’ peers. Whatever is composed on the tongue of anyone will confirm after me that it is poetry. By God, it is true, but they are liars. He said: I said: Enough for me until I go and see. He said: So I came to Mecca and defeated a man from among them, so I said: Where is this man?

Do you call him the Sabian? He pointed at me and said: The Sabian. Then the people of the valley leaned on me with all their arrogance and dignity until I fell unconscious. . . “The hadith mentioned the description of his conversion to Islam, may God be pleased with him, with a Muslim word.

And in the hadith of Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Abu Dharr sent his brother and said: Inform me of the knowledge of this man, whom he claims is coming to him.” The news is from the sky, so listen to what he says, then come to me. The other set off until he came to Mecca, and heard what he said, then returned to Abu Dharr. He said: I saw him enjoining good morals, and speaking words that were not poetic.
He said: You have not cured me of what I wanted, so he took provisions and carried a bag of water for him until he came to Mecca and came to the mosque. . . He mentioned the entire hadith.

On the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, “The Mullahs and Abu Jahl said: We have been defeated by the matter of Muhammad. If you were to seek a man who is knowledgeable in poetry and soothsaying... And magic. He came to him and spoke to him, and he brought us an explanation of its matter.

Utbah bin Rabiah said: By God, I have heard poetry, fortune-telling, and magic, and I have learned knowledge from that, so what is hidden from me is that. So he came to him, and when he came out to him, he said: Are you - O Muhammad - better or Hashem? Are you better than Abdul Muttalib? Are you better or Abdullah? Why do you insult our gods and lead our fathers astray?

If you only have the leadership, then we will appoint the leadership to you, and you will be our head as long as you remain. And if you have the leadership, we will make you marry ten wives that you choose. From whomever of the daughters of Quraysh you wish, and if you have the money, We will gather for you what you and your descendants will be sufficient with afterward, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He was silent and did not speak, then he did not speak

When he finished, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, read: (In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful {Ham - a revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful - a book whose verses are detailed in the Qur’an Arabic for a people who know} [Fussilat: 1-3].
To his saying: {Then say, “I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of Ad and Thamud” [Fussilat: 13].

Then Utbah held his mouth, and pleaded with the relatives to stop, and returned to his family, but he did not go out to the Quraysh, so Utbah withdrew from them, so he said Abu Jahl: O people of Quraysh, by God, we never saw Utbah except that he came to Muhammad and liked his food, and that was only out of need. It struck him, so they went with us to him, and Abu Jahl came to him and said: O Utbah, the only thing that kept you away from us was that you were eager to see Muhammad, and he liked you. His order: If you have a need, we will collect for you from our money what will replace the need for Muhammad’s food. He became angry and swore never to speak to Muhammad again. And he said:
You know that I am one of the wealthiest of the Quraysh, but I came to him and told him the story, and he answered me with something, and by God, he is neither poetic nor Fortune-telling or magic:
{A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, a Book whose verses are explained in detail, an Arabic Qur’an for a people who know} [Fussilat: 1].
To his saying: {Then say, “I warn you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of Ad and Thamud” [Fussilat: 13].

So I grabbed his mouth and called on him to stop, and you knew that when Muhammad said something he did not lie, so I was afraid that the torment would befall you.” It was narrated by Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Mardawayh, in the Book of Interpretation, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Fudayl, on the authority of Al-Ajlah, on the authority of Dhiyāl ibn Harmala, on the authority of him,

It was narrated by Yahya bin Mu’in on the authority of Muhammad bin Fudayl, and Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili narrated it in his Musnad, and Abd bin Humaid narrated it on the authority of Abu’s sheikh Ali Ibn Abi Shaybah.

And in some ways: “If you claim that these people are better than you, then they have worshiped the gods, and if you claim that you are better than them, then speak until We listen.” Ibn Ishaq narrated it, saying: Yazid bin Ziyad, a client of Banu Hashim, narrated to me on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b. He said: It was narrated that Utbah bin Rabia and he was a forbearing gentleman. . He mentioned the hadith until he said: “When he sat with them, they said: What is behind you, Abu Al-Walid?” He said:

What I think is that - by God - I have heard a saying the like of which I have never heard before, and by God, it is not poetry, magic, or divination, O people of Quraysh. Obey me, and do it to me. Leave this man alone with what he is in, and separate from him. By God, what I heard will be a report. The Arabs afflict him, and you have suppressed him with others, and if he prevails over the Arabs, his kingdom is your kingdom, and his honor is your honor, and you are the happiest of people because of him. So they said: He charmed you - by God - O Abu Al-Walid, with his tongue and said: This is my opinion for you, so do what you see fit.
Then he mentioned Abu Talib’s poetry praising Utbah in what he said.

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “Damdād came to Mecca, and he was a man of the worst rank, and he was performing ruqyah because of this wind, so he heard Foolish people of Mecca say: Muhammad is crazy. He said: If I had seen this man, perhaps God would heal him at my hands. He said: I found Muhammad, so I said: I will perform ruqyah from this wind, and God heals at the hands of whomever He wills, so come, and Muhammad said:

“Indeed, praise be to God, we praise Him and seek His help. Whoever God guides, none can mislead him, and whoever He leads astray, none can guide him. I bear witness that there is no god but God.” He is alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger, but after that.” He said: “Repeat these words of yours to me.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated them to him three times and said: By God, I have heard the words of the priests, the words of the magicians, and the words of Poets, I have never heard of these words like yours, and they have reached the sleep of the sea.

He said: Give me your hand and I will pledge my allegiance to you on Islam. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to him, and he said: “And on your people,” so he said: And on Get up.” Hadith.

On the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah came to the Prophet, and he recited to him from the Qur’an: {Indeed, God commands justice and goodness and giving kin, and forbids immorality, abomination, and transgression. He exhorts you that you may remember.} [An-Nahl: 90].

He said: Repeat, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, repeated it and said: “By God, indeed it has sweetness, and indeed it has a sweetness to it, and indeed the highest part of it is fruitful, and indeed Below it.
He is a fool, and what does this man say?

In another version: Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited the Qur’an to him, as if it had been a pity for him, so he conveyed that. Abu Jahl came to him and said: Uncle, your people want to collect money for you. He said: Why? He said: To give it to you, for you came to Muhammad to make up for what he had done before. He said: The Quraysh have learned that I am one of the richest among them. He said: So say something about it. He tells your people that you reject him and that you hate him. He said: What should I say?

By God, there is not a man among you who is more knowledgeable about poetry than me, and I do not know more about its lyrics or his poems than I do. By God, he is not like one who says anything of This, by God, there is sweetness to what he says, and there is sweetness to it, and it is fruitful above it, and abundant below it, and it is To rise and what to raise, and indeed to destroy.

What's underneath it? He said: Your people will not be satisfied with you until you say something about it. He said: So let me think about it. When he thought, he said: This is magic that has an effect, preferring it to anything else. Then it was revealed: “Leave me and those whom I have created alone” [Al-Muddaththir: 11] »
It was narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayyub, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of him.

And in another narration: “Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah gathered, along with a group of Quraysh, and he was a senior among them, and he attended the season and said: The delegations The Arabs will attack you therein, and they have heard about the matter of this companion of yours, so agree upon one opinion concerning him and do not differ, for some of you will deny it. Some of you, and some of you rejected the words of others, so they said: So, O Abu Abd Shams, speak up and give us an opinion that we can follow. He said: Rather, you So they said, “And I listen.” They said: We say a soothsayer. He said: He is not a soothsayer. I have seen soothsayers, but what is he in the soothsayer’s bag? So they said: We say Crazy, he said:

He is not insane. We have seen the insane person and know him, but it is not his suffocation, do not quarrel with him, or his whispering. They said: So we say a poet, and he said: He is not a poet. We know poetry by its rak’ah, its hustle, its short, its contracted, and its simplified, so what is it?

With poetry. They said: So we say a magician. He said: He is not a magician. We have seen magicians and their magic, so it is not his breathing or his contract. They said: What do we say, Abu Abd Shams? He said: By God, his speech has sweetness, and its root is a trough, and its branches are a harvest, so you do not say anything of this without it being known that it False, and the most appropriate statement is that you would say: a magician who separates between a man and his father, and between a man and his brother, and between a man and his wife, And between a person and his clan.

So they separated from him, and made them sit with the people when the season came. No one passed by them without warning him and mentioning his matter to him. So God Almighty revealed regarding Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, and that is from His saying:
{Leave me and those I created alone} [Al-Muddaththir: 11].
To his saying: {I will pray to Saqr} [Al-Muddaththir: 26].
And He revealed regarding the group who were with him: {Those who made the Qur’an compact} [Al-Hijr: 91].
That is, types.

Ibn Ishaq narrated, on the authority of an Egyptian sheikh, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith stood up and said: “O people of Quraysh, by God, something has befallen you, the like of which you have never been afflicted with. Muhammad was a young boy among you, he was pleased with you, and he was truthful to you in speech. And he is the greatest of you in honesty, so much so that when you saw gray hair on his temples, and he brought to you what he brought to you, you said: A magician. No - by God - it is not magic. We have seen the magicians and their breathing and knots, and you said: A soothsayer. No - by God - he is not a soothsayer. We have seen the soothsayers and heard their chanting. And you said:

A poet, no - by God - he is not a poet. We have narrated poetry and heard all its types. He shook him, shook him, and Quraizah, and you said: He is crazy, and no - by God - he is not crazy. We have seen the crazy person and it is not by strangling him. And do not confuse it, O people of Quraysh, look into

“What about you, for - by God - a great matter has befallen you.” Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith was one of the devils of Quraysh, and one of those who harmed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. May God bless him and grant him peace, and incite enmity toward him.

He said: Al-Zuhri told me, saying: “I was told that Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, and Al-Akhnas bin Shurayq went out one night to hear from the Messenger of God.” May God’s prayers and peace be upon him, while he was praying at night in his house, and each of them took a seat to listen to it, and each of them did not know where he was. His companion, so they spent the night listening to him until when the morning came, and dawn came, they dispersed. Then they gathered on the road and they blamed each other, and they said to each other:

Do not return, for if one of your foolish people had seen you, you would have caused something to happen to him. Then they left, until, when the second night came, every man returned. He took them to his meeting, and they began to listen to him, until when dawn came, they dispersed, and they were brought together on the road, and they said to one another as he had said. The first time, then they left, and when the night came

The third time, they did so, then they gathered on the road and they pledged not to return. When the morning came, Al-Akhnas bin Shurayq took his staff, then went to Abu Sufyan was in his house and said: Tell me, O Abu Hanzala, what do you think of what you heard from Muhammad? So he said: O Abu Tha’labah, by God, I have I heard things I know, and I know what they mean, so Al-Akhnas said: And I, by whom I swore. Then he left and went to Abu Out of ignorance, he entered his house and said: O Abu Al-Hakam, what do you think of what you heard from Muhammad? He said:

What did you hear? We and the Banu Abd Manaf quarreled. They fed and we fed, and they carried and we carried, and they gave and we gave, then when we knelt down on our knees, and we were like two horses at stake, they said: Among us is a prophet. Revelation comes from heaven, so when will we realize this? We do not believe in God and we will never believe him.”
Likewise, it was narrated on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah that Abu Jahl told him the same thing, and said: I know that what he says is true, but Banu Qusayy said: Here is the meeting.
So we said: Yes, among us is the veiling, so we said: Yes, among us is the watering, so we said: Yes. He mentioned something similar.
They used to send messages to the People of the Book to ask them about his affair, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Muhammad bin Ishaq said: An Egyptian sheikh told me some forty years ago on the authority of Ikrimah, the client of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas said: “The Quraysh sent Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith and Uqba ibn Abi Mu’it to the Jewish rabbis in Medina, and they said to them: Ask them about Muhammad, describe to them his character, and tell them what he said, for they are the People of the First Book, and they have knowledge that we do not have. The Prophets, so they went out until they came to Medina, so they asked the Jewish rabbis about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they described to them his situation and some He and they said:

You are the people of the Torah, and we have come to you to tell us about this companion of ours. He said: Then the Jewish rabbis said to them: “Ask him about three things.” We command you about them, and if he tells you about them, then he is a sent prophet, and if he does not do so, then the man is a hypocrite, so give him your opinion and ask him about it Young men who went away in the first era, what happened to them, for they had a strange story and they asked him about a man who traveled as far as the east. What was his prophecy about the earth and its western parts? They asked him about the spirit. What is it?
If he informs you of that, then he is a prophet, so follow him, and if he does not inform you, then he is a man of intellect, so deal with his matter as you wish.

Then Al-Nadr and Uqba came and came to Mecca ahead of the Quraysh, and said: O people of Quraysh, we have come to you to separate what is between you and Muhammad. We have ordered The Jewish rabbis told us to ask him about matters, so they told them about them. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, inform us. So they asked him about what he had ordered them to do. So he said: To them, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed you, and Gabriel came to him from God with Surah Al-Kahf, in which is the news of what they asked him about. From the matter of young men, and the man who circumambulates, and God says:
{And they ask you about the spirit. Say, “The spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” [Al-Isra: 85].
Ibn Ishaq said: I was informed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, opened the surah and said: {Praise be to God who sent down to His servant the Book} [Al-Kahf: 1].
That means Muhammad, you are my messenger in fulfilling what they asked him about regarding his prophecy.
{And He did not make for itself any straight crookedness} [Al-Kahf: 1].

That is, He sent it down as a ruler; That is, moderate, with no difference in it, and he mentioned the interpretation of the surah to his saying: {Or did you think that the Companions of the Cave and the Ar-Raqim were a wonder among Our signs?} [Al-Kahf: 9].
That is, what they have destined for My destiny, and what I have done in the affairs of creation, and what My proof I have placed upon my servants, is not greater than that.
Mujahid said: “No one is more astonishing than our signs.”
In Al-Awfi’s interpretation on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The knowledge, the Sunnah, and the Book I have given you are better than the Companions of the Cave.”

I said: The matter is as the predecessors mentioned, for the story of the Companions of the Cave is one of the signs of God, for they remained asleep without dying for three hundred years. A verse indicating God’s power and will, and that He creates whatever He wills, not as the people of atheism say. It is a sign for the eternal return, as God Almighty said: {And thus We caused them to know that the promise of God is true and that the Hour is of which there is no doubt} [Al-Kahf: 21].
The people had a dispute in their time: Should souls be restored rather than bodies?

Telling the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, their story without someone teaching him a sign of his prophecy, so their story was a sign of the foundations of faith. The three; Faith in God, the Last Day, and faith in His Messenger. Despite this, they are not among the signs of God that are astonishing, but rather among the signs of God that are more wondrous than that.

God Almighty mentioned their question about the verses that they were asking Him about in order to know: Is he a true prophet or a liar? Then God Almighty said: {And they will ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn} [Al-Kahf: 83].
And he said: “Indeed, there were signs for Joseph and his brothers for those who ask.” [Joseph: 7].
To his saying: {This is of the tidings of the unseen which We have revealed to you, and you were not with them when they agreed upon their affair while they were plotting} [Yusuf: 102].
To his saying: {And there is no sign in the heavens and the earth. They pass over it, yet they turn away from it. And most of them do not believe in God except And they are polytheists} [Yusuf: 105].

To his saying: {Have they not traveled through the earth and seen what was the end of those before them? And the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who feared. Will they not? Do you understand that when the messengers despaired and thought that they were lied to, Our help would come to them, so we would save whomever We wished, and Our punishment would not be averted from the people. The criminals - indeed, in their stories there is a lesson for those of understanding. It is not a fabricated hadith, but the truthfulness of what is before it and the detailing of everything is guidance. And a mercy for a people who believe.” [Yusuf: 109].

And God Almighty said when He mentioned the story of the People of the Cave about which they asked Him: {And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, “I will recite to you from him.” Remembrance} [Al-Kahf: 83].
That is, they ask you about that, and they ask you about this.

The Qur’an is full of information about the past unseen, which no human being knows, except through the prophets to whom it was told. Therefore, God is not the thing that the philosopher’s atheists claim, for these specific, detailed unseen matters are not taken into account. It was never known about it except from a prophet, such as Moses and Muhammad, and not anyone who claims revelations. Neither one of God’s saints, nor anyone other than God’s saints, can tell of any of that; For this reason, this is one of the signs and characteristics of the prophets, in which no one else shares them.

The people of religion agree on what clear reason has shown, that this is not known except through the news of a prophet. So, if Muhammad was informed of that what Moses and other prophets were informed of, and he was informed of what they know that no one else knows, Except by learning from them, and it was known that Muhammad did not learn this from humans. This was a sign and conclusive proof of his prophethood.

Then the knowledge that Muhammad did not learn this from a human being occurred during his life, as for his people who were directly with him, and who were aware of his situation, they were They know that he did not learn this from humans, so the argument is established against them for that, but he who does not know his condition except by hearing knows that. In ways:

Among them: the frequency of news about him, and how was he? From the time he was born until he died, as it is extensive, well-known and repeated, it is known to those who have had experience with it, greater than what he knows about it. The situation of Moses and Jesus, for Muhammad’s affairs became known, news of him spread, and his circumstances continued. He was greater than all the sons of Adam. What remains of his conditions other than this are hidden from people, so how can something like this be? !

Among them: He was told in the Qur’an something that is not found among the People of the Book, such as: the story of Hud, Salih, and Shuaib, and some details in the story of Abraham, Moses and Jesus; Like the words of Christ in the cradle, and like the descending of the table, this is not known to the People of the Book, and like the faith of Pharaoh’s wife, And other than that. So it cannot be said: He learned this from the People of the Book, and his people did not know that. Rather, he showed them and others traces of it. The warners whom God punished when they denied the messengers, such as the people of Ad and Thamud, and others.

People use existing traces as evidence of the truthfulness of the messengers, and God’s punishment for those who disbelieve them. His people and others use as evidence his sincerity in what he was told of these matters, which he did not learn from the People of the Book, by believing the People of the Book. The book is for him regarding what he agreed with them about, even though they know that he did not learn that from them, and this is what indicates that he did not learn that from them. The People of the Book are something as some of them might think, and that is from both sides, as mentioned above.

Among them: that most of his people were among the people who were most hostile to him, keen to disbelieve and challenge him, and searching for something to slander him. In it. If he had learned this news from humans, they would have known that, slandered him and revealed it, and this would have been one of the things that He appears greater than anyone else. When that did not happen, it indicates that they did not know that, and were not able to slander him despite their knowledge of his condition, and their desire. In the mug with it.

With the perfection of the cause and the power, the One who is capable must exist. When their cause was perfect, and they did not succeed, it is known that this was due to their inability. Their inability to pronounce the curse despite their knowledge of his condition is evidence that they knew that he did not learn it from humans.

Among them: to say: If something like this had happened, it would have been one of the greatest efforts and reasons available for transmitting it. Rather, those who followed it would have If those who believe in it become aware of this, they must spread it and announce it, so what about those who oppose it, those who disbelieve in it?

For the dispersed people who do not conspire, just as they do not come together to intentionally lie, do not come together to conceal something like that, but Kings and presidents strive to conceal what they conceal about the matter of their king, upon whom they have built, and they swear to their guardians to conceal it. That, and they exert their desire and fear in that, and then that becomes apparent, as the inner Qarmatians did, from the people of

Bahrain Bani Ubayd Allah bin Maymun Al-Qaddah, and as people knew that the Nusayriyyah have a speech that they confide to their guardians, even if they do not Most people know what the speech they are talking about is.

Especially those who believed in His praise and followed Him - firstly - among the emigrants. They believed in Him inwardly and outwardly, and they abandoned their homelands for His sake. And family and money, and they were patient with all kinds of hardship and harm: a large group went to Abyssinia,

Migrating with her religion when those who opposed it tortured her until they returned from his religion, and a group were being tortured in Mecca. This man will be killed, and this man will be taken out to Batha Mecca in the heat, and a rock will be placed on his stomach until he disbelieves. This man will be deprived of his sustenance and he will be abandoned. Hungry and naked.

Then they left the country they loved best, and the best for them: Mecca - the Mother of Qura - for a city where they were in need of its people. And they left their wealth in Mecca. God Almighty said: {For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty from Allah. and satisfaction, and they help Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful.” [Al-Hashr: 8].

And God Almighty said: {Permission has been given to those who fight because they have been wronged, and indeed, God is able to grant them victory. Those who have been expelled from their homes without justification, unless... They say, “Our Lord is God.” [Al-Hajj: 39].

And God Almighty said: {So those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes and were harmed in My Way and fought and were killed - I will certainly remit their evil deeds from them. And I will certainly admit them to Gardens beneath which rivers flow, a reward from God, and with God is the best of reward.} [Al Imran: 195].
And His saying: {They will expel the Messenger and you} [Al-Mumtahana: 1].
And all the Muhajireen and Ansar believed in him voluntarily and voluntarily, before anyone was ordered to fight.

He remained in Mecca for some ten years without fighting anyone, nor was he commanded to fight. Rather, he did not force anyone to follow the religion, as God Almighty said: {No. Compulsion in religion. Indeed, righteousness has become distinct from error.} [Al-Baqarah: 256].

They were a large group of people, and it is known that there were a lot of people who followed a person who brought a religion that no one agreed with, and he asked them to They believe in him and follow him, abandon the religion of their fathers, be patient with people’s enmity and harm, and abandon for his sake whatever souls desire. Family, money, and homeland, and despite that, he did not give any of them money, nor did he have any money to give to them, nor did he appoint anyone as governor, nor did he He has authority to give them, and I do not coerce anyone, not even with a pinch in his skin, let alone a whip, or a staff, or a sword, and he - with That - he says about what he tells them from the unseen:
“God told me about it, no human being told me about it.”

However, if they had known that he had learned it from humans, this would have been something they would say to one another. And it is impossible for them to know that he is a liar and that he learned this from humans, and there is no one among them who would inform of this. Even though they were many, it was not possible for them to conspire to lie and conceal, and indeed there was no reason for them to call them to that. It is impossible that they do not know this, since they are his entourage who are aware of his condition, and they hear the words of his enemies who are aware of his condition.

And the Qur’an was revealed little by little. It was not revealed all at once. Rather, they used to ask it about thing after thing of the unseen among those who believed in it. They were inside him and were informed of his secrets, while he did not know any of that. Then he told them about it, and they were aware of his affairs, news after news. And question after question, and this was in Mecca, and there were none of the scholars of the People of the Book, neither Jews nor Christians, then he migrated to The city, and there are many Jews in it; Qaynuqa, Al-Nadir, and Qurayza, and perhaps they were as much as half of its people, or less or more, and they - also - asked him about the unseen. Which only a prophet knows, and he tells them about it, and recites to them what the polytheists asked him about from the unseen, and what he told them about, And he recites to them this unseen that God revealed to him, and explains that God taught him that, no human being taught it to him, so a group believed in him. From the People of the Book, another group disbelieved in him, and in the two groups there is no one among them who says:

He learned this from us, our brothers, or our counterparts, and you did not read it in our books. Although if he had learned that from them, his elders would have been among them, and if their elders knew that he was a liar he learned it from them, they would refrain. That they believe it inwardly and outwardly, but rather their belief in the first book, and their knowledge of the lie of those who claimed the revelation of a second book and having learned from them, they call them Until they explain his matter, show his lie, and say to the people, “He learned from us.” We told him that, especially with what he did to the Jews. From killing, siege, evacuation, captivity, and other things.

If this had happened, it would have been one of the greatest efforts and reasons available to convey it, transmitted by both those who agreed and disagreed, so why did he not say that? No one, and no one transmitted it, despite the mutawatir narrations that he revealed, known to both the public and the private.

That this is what God told me, no human being told me about it. This was clear and conclusive evidence that these unseen news that are not No one knows it except a prophet to whom God taught it, or someone who learned it from a prophet: it is what God has informed him of, and no human being taught it to him, and this Of the unseen about which God said - in the surah in which the jinn listen to the Qur’an and warn their people therewith - where He said:

{Say: It was revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, “Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur’an that guides to right path.” So we believed in it, and we will not associate with our Lord anyone. And indeed, God Almighty is the forefather of our Lord. He has not taken a companion or a son.} [Al-Jinn: 1].
Until he said:

{And when the servant of God stood up, they called upon him, they almost became a cloud over him. Say, “I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate with Him anyone.” Say, “Indeed, I will not be able to harm you.” Nor is there guidance. Say, “Indeed, no one will give me protection from God, nor will I find any one other than Him alone, except as a message from God and His messages. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, then To Him belongs the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide forever. Until when they see what they are promised, they will know who is the weakest helper and least in number. Say, “If I know what is near Are you promised? Or will my Lord appoint for him a period of time? He knows the unseen, and does not reveal the unseen to anyone except him whom He is pleased with from a messenger, for he walks from before Him and from He watched over him so that he would know that they had conveyed the messages of their Lord, and He encompassed what they had and counted everything in number.} [Al-Jinn:
So God Almighty says: {So let him not reveal his unseen} [Al-Jinn: 26].

It shows that it is an unseen that is added to it and is specific to it, and no one knows it except on his part, in contrast to what is hidden from some people and known to it. Some of them may learn this from each other.

Among the things that the People of the Book asked him about in Medina were issues that were different from the issues that he was asked about while he was in Mecca, as the polytheists of Quraysh were. They send to the Jews in Medina, asking them about Muhammad, and the Jews send questions by which they test his prophecy, and that is like what is in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Anas said: “Abdullah bin Salam came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he arrived at Medina and said: I am asking you. On the authority of three things that no one knows except a prophet:

What will be the first signs of the Hour, and what will be the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, and the child will sometimes turn to its mother and to its father. He said: “Tell me.” Gabriel mentioned above. Abdullah said: That is the enemy of the Jews among the angels. “As for the first signs of the Hour, a fire will gather them from the east to the Morocco, and as for the first food that the people of Paradise will eat, it is the liver of a whale, and as for the child, if the man’s fluid precedes the woman’s fluid. He gives the child to its father, and if the woman’s ejaculation precedes the man’s, the child is given to its mother.” He said:

“I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.” He said: O Messenger of God, the Jews are a confused people. If they knew By my conversion to Islam, before you asked them about me, they misled me before you, so the Jews came, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: What a man, Abdullah. Among you, they said: Our best and the son of our best, our master and the son of our master, our scholar and the son of our scholar. He said: Have you seen if Abdullah converted to Islam? They said: May God protect him from that, so Abdullah went out to them and said: “I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness
“Muhammad is the Messenger of God.” They said, “Our evil and the son of our evil,” and they disparaged him. He said, “This is what I feared and was wary of.”

Muslim narrated - in his Sahih - on the authority of Thawban who said: “I was standing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when one of the Jewish rabbis came. He said: “Peace be upon you, O Muhammad.” I pushed him so hard that he almost collapsed. He said: Why do you push me? He said: I said: Don’t you say, O Messenger of God? He said: It’s just I named him by the name by which his family called him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My name by which my family called me is Muhammad. He said: The Jew, I came to ask you, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Something would benefit you if I spoke to you. He said:

I hear with my ears, so he touched a stick with him, and he said to him: Ask. The Jew said: “Where will the people be on the day the earth and the heavens will be changed for another earth?” He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: In the darkness below the bridge, he said: Who is the first among people to leave? He said: The poor immigrants. The Jew said: What will be their gift when they enter? He said: The increase in the liver of Nun. He said: And what is their food?

As a result? He said: The bull of Paradise, which used to eat from its outskirts, will be slaughtered for them. He said: What will they drink of it? He said: From a spring in it called Salsabil. He said: You are right. He said: I have come to ask you about something that no one on earth knows except a prophet or one or two men. He said: It will benefit you if I told you. He said: I hear with my ears. He said: I came to ask you about the child. He said: A man’s semen is white, and a woman’s semen is yellow. So when they come together So, if the man’s semen is superior to the woman’s semen, they will be male, God willing, and if the woman’s semen is superior to the man’s semen, they will be female, God willing. He said:

The Jew said, “You have told the truth, and indeed you are a prophet.” Then he left. He said: The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “He asked me this thing that he asked me about, and I did not know anything about it until God Almighty brought it to me.”

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated that Abd al-Hamid ibn Bahram told us, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “A gang came One day from the Jews to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: O Messenger of God, tell us about something we ask you about that only a prophet knows. He said: Ask me whatever you want, but make me under the protection of God, and Jacob did not charge his sons if I told you something that you know is true. That you may follow me in Islam. They said: That is yours. He said: So ask me whatever you wish. They said:

Tell us about four things: Tell us about the food that Israel forbade itself before the Torah was revealed, and tell us about the man’s water, how is the penis made from it? Until he is a male, and how he is a female until he is a female, and tell us how this Prophet sleeps, and who is your guardian among the angels? He said: Then upon you is God’s covenant and covenant. If I spoke to you, you would follow me. So give him whatever covenant and covenant he wishes. He said:

I adjure you by the One who sent down the Torah to Moses; Do you know that Israel - Jacob - fell seriously ill and was ill for a long time, so he made a vow to God that if God healed him of his illness, he would deprive the women he loved He liked the drink, and he liked the food, and the drink he liked was camel milk, and the food he liked was camel meat. They said: Oh God, yes, so he said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O God, bear witness against them. He said: I adjure you.

By God, there is no god but Him, who sent down the Torah to Moses; Do you know that a man’s water is thick and white, and that a woman’s water is thin and yellow? Whichever is higher, the boy will be born, and the resemblance to him, God willing, They said: Oh God, yes, and he said: Oh God, bear witness. He said: I adjure you by God, besides whom there is no god, and who sent down the Torah to Moses. Do you know that this Prophet’s eyes sleep, but his heart does not sleep? They said: Oh God, yes. He said: Oh God, bear witness. They said: You. Now tell us who Your guardian is one of the angels, then we will have intercourse with you or separate from you. He said:

My guardian is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and God has never sent a prophet except that he is his guardian. They said: Then we will separate from you. If it had been someone other than him, we would have followed you. And we believed you. He said: What prevents you from believing? They said: He is our enemy among the angels. Then God Almighty revealed:
{Whoever is an enemy of Gabriel - indeed, he has sent it down to your heart by God’s leave, confirming it} [Al-Baqarah: 97].
To his saying: {For God is an enemy to the disbelievers} [Al-Baqarah: 98] »

In these hadiths, Jewish scholars such as Abdullah bin Salam and others used to ask him about issues, to which they would say: No. Only a prophet knows it: that is, whoever learned it from the prophets, then the questioners knew it, as it came - also -: “No one knows it except a prophet.” Or one or two men.”

So they used to test him with these issues to determine whether he knew them, and if he knew what only a prophet knew, then he was a prophet and known. What they meant by that would only be achieved if they knew that he did not know these issues from the People of the Book, or from those who learned from them, otherwise It is known that some people learned these matters, but they learned them from the prophets.

This shows that those asking him from the People of the Book knew that no human being had taught him what the People of the Book had. Science; If they had allowed that to happen to him, their purpose of testing him would not have been achieved. Is he a prophet or not? If they allow that he learned what only a prophet from the People of the Book knew, then he was of their kind, so he had no knowledge of it. Their answer is evidence of his prophecy.

These questioners must be certain that he did not learn from the People of the Book. This was in Medina after he had resided in Mecca for some ten years, and his rule spread, and his people rejected him and were keen to invalidate Calling upon him in every way they are able, if there was in Mecca or in Medina one of the People of the Book who could learn from him, or if he met one of the people of the Book. The People of the Book are on a path, so learn from them. This would have suggested the intention of these questioners.

So it became clear that it was known to the People of the Book that he did not learn anything of the unseen from humans, especially if he had learned it from the People of the Book. The Book, and he denied them and fought them. They would have shown that, and he spread the word among the People of the Book, so when he answered them, they would say: This is what I learned from So-and-so, and so-and-so from among us, or this was taught to you by some of the people of our religion. This is just as they used to send to his people from the Quraysh to ask him about matters, and they would say: If he informs you of them then he is a sent prophet. Otherwise, he is a hypocrite, and they say: Ask him about issues that only a prophet knows.

This is from the people of Medina and his people from the Quraysh, which shows that his polytheist people and the People of the Book were in agreement that he had not learned Nothing from that human beings, because if they allowed that, their purpose by that would not have been achieved, and it is not permissible for them to say that only a prophet knows it, For they all knew that among the People of the Book there are those who know these issues, and thus it is known whether he will answer them based on what she said. The prophets, or otherwise, and they know that whoever learned it from the People of the Book, and whoever learned it from them, his answer does not indicate it. on his prophecy as if he had responded to that

The issues are some of the People of the Book, and it is as if in our time some people asked some Muslims about these issues or other news. The unseen, which only a prophet knows, because that does not indicate his prophecy. Because he learned that from the prophets.
This indicates that what they meant when they said: Only a prophet knows it:

That is, no one would know it from the beginning without teaching from a human being except a prophet, and it indicates that the polytheists and the People of the Book were all agreed that He did not learn from anyone with the spread of news of it, and with his people learning about its secrets, and with this appearing - if it existed - and even though they They allowed it to be that he had learned it from a human being inwardly. It was not permissible for it to be used as evidence for his prophecy, so it indicated that they were decisive. Because he did not learn this from humans; Neither inwardly nor outwardly, and this is a clear path that indicates that he did not learn this from humans other than the methods mentioned here.

chapters.title: A chapter on the clarity, diversity, and abundance of the verses of prophecy
paragraphs: [Chapter: The manifestation of the signs of prophecy, their diversity, and their abundance]

And since Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was a messenger to all the heavyweights, the jinn and their humans, the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and he is the Seal of the Prophets - no A prophet after him - it was one of God’s blessings upon His servants, and one of the completeness of His proof upon His creation was that the signs of his prophecy and the proofs of his message were known. For all the creation to whom he was sent, and these people may have signs and proofs of his prophecy that these people do not have.

And he used to show every people psychological and apocalyptic verses by which he made it clear that the Qur’an is the truth, as God Almighty said: {Say, “Have you seen? It was from God, then you disbelieved in it. Who is more astray than he who is in discord far away? We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them. Indeed, it is the truth. Is not your Lord sufficient that He is a witness over all things? [Fussilat: 52].

God Almighty has told that He will show His servants the signs within themselves and on the horizons until it becomes clear to them that the Qur’an is true, for the conscience is returning. to him; Since it is He who mentioned it previously, as He said: {Say, “Have you considered if it is from Allah and then you disbelieve in it? Who is more astray than he who is in distant discord?} [Fussilat: 52]
The pronoun in (kan) refers to something known.

He says: Have you considered that if the Qur’an was from God, and then you disbelieved in it, who is more astray than he who is in deep discord? According to this assessment, the infidel is in a deep discord that has antagonized God and His Messenger, and no one is more astray than one who is in such a discord. Where he was in trouble, while God and His Messenger were in trouble, as God Almighty said:

{Say, “We believe in God and in what was revealed to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what The prophets were given from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit. So if they believe in the same as you believe in, then they are guided. If they turn away, then they are only in discord, so God will suffice you for them, and He is the Hearer, the Knower” [Al-Baqarah: 136].

He made it clear that whoever turned away from that was not following the truth and intending it, for this is what you said, no one from the People of the Book will turn away from it. His intention is the truth, but he who intends opposition and antagonism turns away from it, due to his own desires, and this is sufficient for you, may God protect you.

And if the Qur’an is from God, and then whoever disbelieves in it, then no one is more astray than someone who is in his condition. Since he is in a distant discord, and if it is assumed that he does not know that it is the truth, then he is lost. Disagreement may occur with stubbornness, or it may occur with ignorance, for if the signs appear and he turns away from the view that leads to knowledge, that is hardship. That is why he said after that: {We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth} [Fussilat: 53].

So he informed that he would show his servants of the horizontal and psychological signs that would make it clear that it is the truth, then he said: {Is not your Lord sufficient that He is upon Everything is a witness} [Fussilat: 53].

His testimony alone is sufficient, without the signs that are expected, as God Almighty said: {Say: God is sufficient as a witness between me and you and those who are with Him. Knowledge of the Book} [Al-Ra’ad: 43].

His testimony to the Qur’an and to Muhammad is through his sayings that he revealed before that to his prophets, as God Almighty said about the People of the Book: {And who is more unjust than he who conceals the testimony that he has from God?} [Al-Baqarah: 140].

And it is through his actions, which is the signs and proofs he produces that indicate the truthfulness of his messengers, for he believed them in what they were informed of. About him, and he bore witness to them that they were truthful.

The Qur’an - itself - is the word of God, and it contains God’s testimony for what the Messenger informed him of, and what was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And bringing it to Muhammad is a sign and proof, and that is from the action of God. Since human beings were not able to do anything like it, none of the prophets, nor the saints, nor the magicians, nor anyone else could do it, as He said. God Almighty: {Say, “If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they would not produce the like of it, even if they were to support one another.” At noon} [Al-Isra: 88].
Muhammad was informed of this at the beginning of his command, as this verse was in Surah (Glory be to Him), which is Meccan.

He issued it in remembrance of the Night Journey that took place in Mecca, by people’s agreement. He told the news and confirmed it with an oath on behalf of all the two heavy creatures - forget them and their jinn - that if they gathered together, they would produce something like this. They do not produce anything like it, rather they are unable to do so, and this contains signs of his prophecy.

Among them is his presenting this great news about all mankind and jinn until the Day of Resurrection that they will not do this, but rather They are unable to do so. This is something that someone who asks people to believe him does not do unless he is confident that the matter is so. If he had any doubt about that, it would be permissible for him to show that he lied in this report, thus ruining what he intended, and this would not be the case. sane with the agreement of the nations; The believer in Muhammad, and the disbeliever in him, despite the perfection of his mind, knowledge, and experience, since he ruled the world with a policy that no one else had ruled. With the same.

Then He made this in the recited Qur’an that is preserved until the Day of Resurrection, which is read in prayers, and is heard by both the public and the private. The guardian and the enemy are evidence of his complete confidence in the truth of this news. Otherwise, if he had doubts about it, he would fear that his lie would be revealed when He has many people, but most of those who followed him and those who were hostile to him, and this is not done by someone who intends for people to believe him. People believe him, he does not say something like this, he makes this appearance, he spreads this rumor, and this immortality immortalizes him, except... He is certain of his honesty.

It is inconceivable that a human being would be certain of this news unless he knew that this is something that creation is incapable of, since the world knows of the inability of all mankind and jinn until the Day of Resurrection, is one of the greatest indications of its being miraculous, and of its being a sign of his prophecy. This is one of the indications His prophecy was first heard by those who heard these words and knew that it was part of the Qur’an, which was commanded to be conveyed to all of creation, and He alone It is sufficient to know that the Qur’an is miraculous.

Leave aside the many other indications that it is miraculous, such as the inability of all nations to oppose it with complete desire and keenness. To oppose him, and failure to act with the perfection of the motive entails lack of ability, so since the motives of the Arabs and others for opposition were complete, he knew The inability of all nations when they opposed him, and this is a second proof by which the truth of this news is known, and the truth of this news is a sign of his prophecy beyond Knowing that the Qur’an is miraculous, is an independent sign of its prophecy, and it is a clear sign that will remain until the end of time, known to everyone. One, and it is one of the greatest verses.
