The fact that it is a miracle is known through multiple proofs, and the miracle has multiple faces, so the evidence for its miraculousness varied, and its faces varied. His miraculousness, and every aspect of it is indicative of his miraculousness. These are sentences that would be extended in detail. For this reason, the Almighty said: {And they say, “Why have signs not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The signs are only with God, and I am only a clear warner. Is not that sufficient for them?” Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book, which will be recited to them. Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.} [Al-Ankabut: 50].
It is sufficient in advocacy and clarification, and it is sufficient in argument and proof.

chapters.title: Chapter investigating the name of the miracle, the sign, and the dignity and their release
paragraphs: [Chapter: Investigating the name of the miracle, the sign, the dignity, and their application]

The verses and proofs that indicate the prophecy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are many and varied, and they are more and greater than the verses of any other verse. Prophets, and the theorists call them (miracles), and they are called (evidence of prophecy) and (signs of prophecy).

If these words were called the verses of the prophets, they would be more indicative of what is meant by the word miracles, and for this reason the word “miracles” was not used. (Miracles) are present in the Qur’an and Sunnah, but it contains the word (verse), (clear evidence), and (proof), as God Almighty said in the story Moses: {Then these are two proofs from your Lord} [Al-Qasas: 32].

In the staff and the hand, and God Almighty said regarding Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: {O people, there has come to you proof from your Lord, and We have sent down To you is a clear light} [An-Nisa: 174].

He said in asking the people of false claims for proof: {And they say, “None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian.” That is Their aspirations: Say, “Bring your proof, if you are truthful” [Al-Baqarah: 111].

And the Almighty said: {Is it not who initiates creation, then returns it, and who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? A god with God. Say, “Bring your proof, if you are.” truthful} [An-Naml: 64].
And he said: {And whoever invokes with God another god for which he has no proof - his account is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.} [Al-Mu’minun: 117].

And God Almighty said: {And on the Day when He calls them and says, “Where are my partners whom you claimed?” And We removed from every nation a witness, so We said, “Bring your proof.” So they knew that the truth belongs to Allah, and that which they had invented has gone away from them” [Al-Qasas: 74].

As for the word (verses), it is abundant in the Qur’an, such as the Almighty’s saying: {And thus We have placed in every town the worst of its criminals to plot in it, and what They plot only against themselves, and they do not perceive. And when a sign comes to them, they say, “We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the Messengers of God. God knows best where we will be.” He makes His message} [Al-An'am: 123].
And the Almighty said: {And We gave Moses nine clear signs} [Al-Isra: 101].
And God Almighty said: {And put your hand into your pocket, and it will come out white without blemish} [An-Naml: 12] another verse.
And Pharaoh said to him: “Then bring it if you are of the truthful” [Al-Shu’ara: 31].

And Salih’s people said to him: “Then bring a sign, if you are of the truthful ones.” He said, “This is a she-camel. She will have water, and you will have water on an appointed day.” [Al-Shu’ara’: 154].
And he said: {This is the she-camel of God as a sign for you} [Al-A`raf: 73].

And Christ said: {I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. Indeed, I create for you out of clay the likeness of a bird, then I blow into it and it becomes a bird, God willing. And I will heal the blind and the lepers, and I will bring the dead to life by God’s leave, and I will inform you of what you shall eat and what you shall store in your houses. Indeed, in that A sign for you, if you are believers.} [Al Imran: 49].

And he said regarding Muhammad: {And not a sign of their Lord comes to them but they turn away from it. Indeed, they have denied the truth when it has come to them. There will come to them news of what they used to mock.} [Al-An'am: 4].
{The Hour has drawn near and the moon has been split, and if they see a sign they will turn away and say, “Continuous magic.” [Al-Qamar: 1].

And He said: {And among them is he who listens to you, and We have placed over their hearts a veil, lest they understand it, and deafness in their ears. And if they see every sign, they will not believe. Until, when they come to you, they dispute with you. Those who disbelieve say, “These are nothing but legends of ancient peoples.” [Al-An’am: 25].

And God Almighty said: {And they say, “Why have signs not been sent down to him from his Lord?” Say, “The signs are only with God, and I am only a clear warner. Is not that sufficient for them?” We have sent down to you the Book, which will be recited to them. Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.} [Al-Ankabut: 50].
And he said: {We will show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth} [Fussilat: 53].

And God Almighty said: {Indeed, there is a sign for you regarding two groups that meet. One group fights in the way of God and the other is disbelieving. They will see them as the same as they are, the sight of the eye. And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those with insight.} [Al Imran: 13].

And God Almighty said: {And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who do not hope for the meeting with Us say, “Bring a Qur’an other than this, or alter it.” Say, “It is not for me.” To change it of my own accord} [Yunus: 15].
And the Almighty said: {Say, “Look, ‘Look what is in the heavens and the earth,’ and the signs and warnings are of no avail for a people who do not believe.” [Yunus: 101].

And he said, when he mentioned the stories of the prophets in Surat Ash-Shu’ara’ - he said at the end of each story: {Indeed, in that is a sign, and most of them were not believers - and indeed Your Lord is the Mighty, the Most Merciful} [Al-Shu’ara’: 67-68].
And he said: “Indeed, there were signs for Joseph and his brothers for those who ask.” [Joseph: 7].
Until he said at the end of it: {This is from the news of the unseen which We have revealed to you, and you were not with them when they gathered their affair and were plotting} [Yusuf: 102].
To his saying: {And there is every sign in the heavens and the earth. They pass over it, but they turn away from it} [Yusuf: 105].

And God Almighty said: {Allah has promised you many spoils that you will take, so He hastened these for you and restrained the hands of people from you, and that they might be a sign for the believers.} [Al-Fath: 20] .
And He said: {And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We gave them shelter to a mountain full of stability and well-being.} [Al-Mu’minun: 50].
As for the word miraculous, it only indicates that he is more incapable than anyone else, as God Almighty said: {And they are not miraculous} [Az-Zumar: 51].
And He said: {And you are not inimitable on earth or in heaven} [Al-Ankabut: 22].

And whoever does not affirm that an action belongs to anyone other than God says: The miracle is God, but someone else is called a miracle metaphorically. This wording does not indicate that this is a sign or proof unless what is meant by it is explained and its conditions are mentioned, and for this reason many of the theologians He does not call anything miraculous except what was for the prophets only, and what was for the saints if it is proven that they violated a custom that he called dignity.

And the predecessors - like Ahmad and others - used to call this and that a miracle, and they said of the miracles of the saints: They are miracles, since there were none in them. The wording is something that requires the prophets to be specific to that. Other than what was a sign and proof of the Prophet’s prophecy, this must be singled out.

They may call the miracles signs, because they indicate the prophecy of the one whom the Guardian followed. The proof is necessary for the meaning, and it cannot be proven. Without the meaning being proven, likewise what was a sign and proof, which is evidence and knowledge of the Prophet’s prophecy, cannot be for anyone other than the Prophet. The extension of this has another place.

What is meant here is that the evidence for the prophecy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is many and varied, as we have talked about elsewhere in this book. We have made clear that whoever specifies the evidence of prophecy to one type has made a mistake. Rather, there are many types, but the verses are of two types: and among them: what has passed. It became known by news, like the miracles of Moses and Jesus.

Among them: what has survived to this day, like the Qur’an, which is one of the signs of the prophecy of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and like the knowledge and faith that are in His followers, for it is one of the signs of his prophecy, and like his law that he brought, it is - also - one of the signs of his prophecy, and like the verses that God reveals it time after time as a result of the blessings of the righteous among His nation, and the occurrence of what He informed of its occurrence, such as His saying: “The Hour will not come until “You fight the Turks,” and his saying: “The Hour will not come until a fire emerges from the land of Hijaz, illuminating the necks of the camels in Busra.”
This fire came out in the year six hundred and sixty-five, and people saw the necks of camels in Busra.

His religion and religion emerged through argument and proof, hand and tongue, examples and punishments that befall his enemies, and other than that. His similitude is found in the books of the prophets before him, and other than that.

chapters.title: A chapter examining the Qur’anic miracle
paragraphs: [Chapter: Research into the Qur’anic miracle]

The Qur’an is the word of God, and in it is the call and the argument, so it has jurisdiction over others, as it is proven from him in the Sahih that he said: “There is no prophet who Prophets, except that he was given signs, the likes of which humans believed. Rather, what I was given was a revelation that God revealed to me, so I hope that I will be He will be the one who follows the most on the Day of Resurrection.”

The Qur’an appears to be a sign and proof of it in several ways: both in general and in detail. As for the sentence, it has been known to the elite and the common people among the nations, with frequent knowledge that it is he who brought this Qur’an. And the frequency of that news was greater than the frequency of the news of every one of the prophets, kings, philosophers, and others.

The Qur’an itself contains a challenge to the nations with opposition, and the challenge is to challenge them: that is, to call them and send them to They oppose him, so it is said about him: He led me on this matter: that is, he sent me on it, and from him it was called Hadi Al-Ais; Because he alone sends her on the road.

Some people may want to challenge the claim of prophecy, but it is its primary origin. God Almighty said: In Surat Al-Tur: {Or do they say it is His saying? Nay, no. If they believe, let them bring a hadith like it, if they are truthful.} [At-Tur: 33].
Here he said: {Then let them produce a hadith like it, if they are truthful} [At-Tur: 34].

In that he recited it, then if Muhammad was able to recite it as a human being is able to speak in the manner in which he speaks And in prose, this was possible for the people, who were of his kind, so it enabled the people to come up with something like him.

Then He challenged them with ten surahs like it, and God Almighty said: {Or do they say, “He has fabricated it?” Say, “Then produce ten forged surahs like it, and call upon those who You are able to other than God, if you are truthful.} [Hud: 13].

Then he challenged them with one surah from it, and God Almighty said: {And this Qur’an was not to be fabricated other than Allah, but to confirm what is before it. And the details of the Book, about which there is no doubt, are from the Lord of the worlds - or do they say, “He fabricated it?” Say, “Then produce a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah.” You were truthful} [Yunus: 37-38].

So he asked them to produce ten surahs like it, inventions of themselves and everyone they could besides God, then he challenged them with one surah. They and those who are able, He said: {Then if they do not respond to you, then know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God and that there is no god but Him} [Hud: 14].
This is the origin of his call, which is the testimony that there is no god but God, and the testimony that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.
And God Almighty said: {But if they do not respond to you, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of God} [Hud: 14].
As he said: {But God bears witness of what has been revealed to you. He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness} [An-Nisa: 166].
That is: He knows that it was revealed, but he does not know that it was forged, as He said: {And this Qur’an should not have been forged besides Allah} [Yunus: 37].

That is: He would not have been slandered. He says: He would not have done this. He did not deny merely doing it, rather he denied the possibility of doing it, and stated that something like this does not happen, rather it is prevented from happening, so the meaning is: What It is possible, but it is not possible, and it is not permissible for this Qur’an to be fabricated instead of God, for the one who fabricates it other than God is a created being, and a created being is not He is able to do that. This challenge took place in Mecca, as these surahs are Meccan. Surat Yunus, Hud, and Surat Al-Tur.

Then he repeated the challenge in Medina after the Hijra, and said in (Al-Baqarah), which is a Medinan surah: {And if you are in doubt concerning what We have sent down to Our servant. Then produce a surah like it, and call your witnesses besides Allah, if you are truthful.” [Al-Baqarah: 23].
Then he said: {But if you do not do it, and you will not do it, then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones} [Al-Baqarah: 24].
So he mentioned two things: One of them was his saying: {Then if you do not do it, and you will not do it, then fear the Fire} [Al-Baqarah: 24].

He says: If you do not do this, then you know that it is the truth, so fear God, lest you deny it, and then the torment that He has promised to the deniers will befall you. This is a call to the path of his Lord with good advice, after He called them to wisdom, and it is to argue with them in a way that is best.
The second is His saying: “And you will not do it” [Al-Baqarah: 24].

And (not) to negate the future, so the news has been proven that in the future of time, they will not produce a surah like it, as was reported before. That, and he commanded him to say in Surah (Glory be to Him), which is a Meccan surah, which he opened by mentioning the Night Journey, while he was in Mecca, with the text of the Qur’an. And the Mutawatir narrations, in which he mentioned his address to the infidels in Mecca, explaining that by saying: {Say, “If mankind and the jinn were gathered together, Unless they produce the like of this Qur’an, they will not produce the like of it, even if some of them were supportive of one another.} [Al-Isra: 88].

So the news spread to all of creation, astonishing for them, conclusively stating that if they all gathered together, they would not produce the like of this Qur’an, even if they pretended to do so. They cooperated in this, and this challenge and supplication is for all of creation, and this has been heard by everyone who has heard the Qur’an and knows it, private and public, and knows - However - they did not oppose him, nor did they produce a surah like it, and from the time he was sent, and until today, the matter has been like that, despite what has been known of That all of creation were infidels before he was sent, and when he was sent, only a few followed him.

The infidels were among the people most eager to invalidate his words, striving in every way possible, sometimes they went to the People of the Book. So they ask them about matters from the unseen, until they ask him about them, just as they asked him about the story of Joseph, the people of the cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn, as mentioned above. Sometimes they gathered in council after council over what they said about him, and they began to give him parables, likening him to someone who is not like him. Just because of some similarity with the appearance of the difference. Sometimes they say: crazy. Sometimes they say: a magician. Sometimes they say: a priest. Sometimes they say: a poet. . .
And similar statements that they and every sane person who has heard them know are slander against him.

If he had challenged them with opposition - time after time - and it nullified his call, then it is known that if they had been able to do so, They would have done it, for with the existence of this complete and certain motive, if power were to be achieved, the existence of what is destined must be present, then this is the saying in All the people of the earth.

This fate necessitates clear knowledge for everyone of the inability of all the people of the earth to produce the like of this Qur’an by trickery or without A trick. This is more eloquent than the verses whose type is repeated, such as reviving the dead, for no one has ever brought anything like it, and the Qur’an is It is not a miracle in terms of its eloquence and eloquence only, or its organization and style only, nor in terms of its telling of the unseen only. Not only in terms of diverting the reasons for opposing it, nor in terms of taking away their ability to oppose it only, but rather it is a clear and miraculous sign. In many ways:

In terms of pronunciation, in terms of structure, in terms of eloquence in the meaning of the word, and in terms of its meanings that it conveys about God. God Almighty, His names, His attributes, His angels, and so on.

With regard to its meanings, with which it told about the past unseen, and about the future unseen, and with regard to what it told about the Day of Resurrection, and from In terms of the certain proofs that He has made clear in it, and the rational analogies that are the given proverbs, as God Almighty said: {And We have explained There is every example in this Qur’an for people in this Qur’an, but most people refuse, except as disbelievers.} [Al-Isra: 89].
And God Almighty said: {And We have presented in this Qur’an every example for mankind, but man is the most contentious of all things} [Al-Kahf: 54].
And he said: {And We have given the people in this Qur’an every example that they may remember - an Arabic Qur’an, not crooked, that they may be righteous.} [Az-Zumar: 27] - 28].

Everything that people mentioned regarding the aspects of the miraculous nature of the Qur’an is evidence of its miraculousness, and there is no contradiction in that. Rather, every people was aware of what Pay attention to him.

Among the weakest statements is that of the people of theology who say: It is miraculous by eliminating the reasons - with the complete reason for them - or by taking away the power. Completely, or by robbing them of the ability that is usual in a similar situation in a general manner, such as the Almighty saying to Zechariah: {I sign that you will not speak to people for three nights. Together} [Maryam: 10].

And it is that God turned the hearts of the nations away from opposing Him with the fulfillment of the complete requirement. This is said by way of decree and revelation, which is that if it is decreed that this speech will enable people to come up with something similar to it, Their abstention - all of them - from this opposition, despite the existence of great reasons for opposition, is one of the most eloquent of the miraculous signs. For customs, like someone who says:

I am taking the money of all the people of this great country, beating them all, and starving them, and they are able to complain until God, or to the guardian, and none of them complains, for this is one of the most extraordinary miracles.

If it were assumed that someone wrote a book, others like him would be able to write a similar book, or if he wrote poetry, people like him would be able to write the same, He challenged them all, and said: Oppose me, and if you do not oppose me, then you are infidels. Your abode is Hell, and your blood is permissible for me. He usually refrained from not Someone opposes him. If they did not oppose him, this would be one of the most extraordinary miracles.

And the one who brought the Qur’an said to all of creation: I am the Messenger of God to all of you, and whoever believes in me will enter Paradise, and whoever does not believe in me will enter Hell, and he It is permissible for me to kill their men, take captive their descendants, and take the spoils of their wealth. They are all obligated to obey me, and whoever does not obey me is among the most wretched. creation, and among My signs is this Qur’an, for no one is able to bring the like of it, and I tell you that no one can bring the like of it.
It is said: It is not the case that people are either able or incapable of dissent.

If they were able, and did not oppose him, then God diverted the desires of their hearts and prevented them from wanting to oppose him with this great challenge, or rob them of them. The ability that was in them before his challenge, for taking away the usual ability for a man to say: My miracle is that all of you are unable to control anyone. Some of you are not allowed to speak or to eat or drink, for preventing something that is accustomed is like doing something that is not accustomed to - this is one of the most profound miracles.

And if they are unable, it is proven that it is extraordinary, so it is proven that it is extraordinary based on the estimation of the two opposites. Denial and affirmation. It has been proven that it is one of the wonders that contradicts custom in the same matter.

This is the purpose of the revelation. Otherwise, what is absolutely correct is that all of creation is incapable of opposing Him. They are not able to do that, nor are they able to do so. Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was able, on his own initiative, to replace a chapter of the Qur’an. Indeed, the difference between the Qur’an and The rest of his words are for everyone who has the slightest contemplation, as God has told him in his saying.
{Say, “If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an, they would not produce the like of it, even if they were to help one another.} [Al-Isra: 88]
Also, people find their reasons for opposition occurring, but they feel within themselves their inability to oppose, even if they were able Those who opposed him.

He appointed more than one person to oppose him, but he came with words in which he exposed himself and demonstrated the fulfillment of what the Qur’an reported of his inability. creation by bringing something like it, such as the liar Qur’an of Musaylimah, such as his saying: (O frog, daughter of two frogs, purify as much as you purify, not the water You disturb, and you do not prevent the drinker, your head is in the water, and your tail is in the mud.)

Likewise - also - they know that their state of ability did not differ before hearing it and after hearing it, so they do not find themselves unable to do anything. They were able to control him, just as Zechariah found himself unable to speak after being able to control him.

Also, there is no dispute between the wise people who believe in Muhammad and those who deny him. His intention was for people to believe him and not disbelieve him, and he was with He is one of the wisest people, the most knowledgeable, and the most knowledgeable of what he brought. He will achieve what he intended, whether it is said: He is telling the truth or a liar. Whoever called the people to such a great matter, and continued until they responded to him willingly or unwillingly, and his call appeared and spread... He was bored by this spread. He was one of the great men, in any case.

With this intention, he came forward - with this intention - at the beginning of the matter while he was in Mecca, and his followers were few, provided that he narrated news, which makes it certain that if Mankind and the jinn have gathered together to produce the like of this Qur’an. They will not produce anything like it, neither in that era nor in any other era.

It is only when he is certain of that and is certain of it, otherwise he is in doubt and suspicion. He who fears that it will appear should not say that. His lie is exposed and people stop believing him.

If he was certain of that - and certain of it - then that was only because God informed him of that. It is not in the usual sciences that a person should know that all of creation are not able to produce words like his unless the scholar knows that Beyond human ability. Knowing this requires that it is miraculous, for we know that even if our knowledge of that is not extraordinary, but it requires those who Knowledge is the confirmation of what is known, and if knowledge is ignorance, then it is proven that it is proven, in every estimation, that it is supernatural.

As for the details, it is said: The exact structure of the Qur’an and its style are strange and wonderful, not of the type of known methods of speech, and no one came In view of this style, it is not of the same type as poetry, rhyme, oratory, or messages, and it is not structured like any of the people’s Arabic speech. And their diction, and the same eloquence and eloquence of the Qur’an, this is wondrous and extraordinary. It has no counterpart in the speech of all creation. And the extension of this Its details are long, and those who have insight and contemplation will know it.

The same thing that the Qur’an told us about in the chapter on the oneness of God and His names and attributes is a strange and extraordinary matter. There has never been anything like that in The words of a human being, neither a prophet nor a non-prophet.

Likewise, what he told about the angels, the throne, the throne, the jinn, the creation of Adam, and other than that, and the same thing that the Qur’an commanded about Religion, and the laws as well, and the same as what he told of parables, and the evidence he showed is - also - like that.

Whoever ponders what all wise people have classified in the divine, moral and political sciences will find that he is in line with what is stated in the divine books - The Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Books of the Prophets - there was a greater discrepancy between these and the Qur’an than between its wording and its structure, and between All Arab words and their systems.

The miracle in its meaning is greater and more numerous than the miracle in its wording, and all the wise people of the nations are incapable of coming up with its meanings. Greater than the inability of the Arabs to come up with a word similar to it. And what is in the Torah and the Gospel:

Even if it is assumed that it is like the Qur’an, it does not detract from its meaning, then those are the books of God - also - and it is not impossible for a prophet to come with a verse equivalent to it. A prophet, just as Christ came to revive the dead, and the resurrection of the dead occurred at the hands of others; So how come when what is in the Torah and the Gospel is not identical to the meanings of the Qur’an? Not in reality, nor in quality, nor quantity, but rather the discrepancy appears to everyone who contemplates the Qur’an and the books.

And these matters are apparent to those of the people of knowledge and knowledge, its miracle will become apparent to them in this respect, and to those to whom it does not appear That was enough for the apparent matter that appeared to him and others like him, such as the inability of all creation to come up with something like it, despite the challenge of the Prophet. And informing him of their inability, as this is apparent to everyone.

The evidence of prophecy is of the same type as the evidence of divinity, in which is apparent and clear to everyone; Such as witnessed incidents; Such as the creation of animals, plants, clouds, and the sending of rain, and so on, and it includes what is specific to those who know them, such as the details of anatomy. And the magnitudes of the planets and their movements, and so on. All of creation is in need of acknowledgment of the Creator and acknowledgment of His messengers, and what The need for him is great in religion and this world, for God bestows universal generosity on His servants through him.

Since their need for life was greater than their need for water, and their need for water was greater than their need for food, it was Glory be to Him, He brought the air as universal goodness in every place and time due to the need of animals for it, then water without it, but it exists more than what is found. Sustenance is easier; Because the need for it is greater.

Likewise are the evidences of divinity, the greatest need of creation for it in their religion, then the evidences of prophecy; For this reason, God has made it easy and made it easier than what the common people do not need, such as the symmetry and difference of bodies, the persistence of symptoms or Its annihilation, the persistence of the individual essence or its disappearance, such as the issues of the woman suffering from istihaadah, the cessation of the Hajj and its invalidation, and other such things that he talks about. There are some scholars in it.

chapters.title: Detailing the personality of the Messenger, his law, his nation, and the honors of the righteous among them are all from His verses
paragraphs: [Chapter: The personality of the Messenger, his law, his nation, and the blessings of the righteous among them, all of that is among His signs.]

The biography of the Messenger, his morals, his words, his actions, and his law are among his signs, and his nation is among his signs, and the knowledge of his nation and their religion are among his signs, And the blessings of righteousness of his nation are among His signs. This is evident by examining his biography from the time he was born until he was sent, and from where he was sent until he died, and examining his lineage and country. And his origin and origin, he was one of the most noble people of the earth by lineage, from the very lineage of Abraham, in whose descendants God granted prophecy. And the Book: No prophet came after Abraham except from his descendants, and We will give him two sons:

Ishmael and Isaac, and this and that was mentioned in the Torah, and he was given good tidings in the Torah about what would be among the progeny of Ishmael, but he was not among the progeny of Ishmael. Whoever appeared in what the prophecies heralded was others, and Abraham called for the descendants of Ishmael to send among them a messenger from among themselves, then from the Quraysh. The elite of the Banu Ibrahim, then from the Banu Hashim the elite of the Quraysh, and from Mecca, the mother of Al-Qura and the city of the House that Abraham built, and he called the people to His Hajj, and it was still a Hajj since the time of Abraham, mentioned in the books of the prophets with the best description.

He was one of the most complete people in upbringing and upbringing. He was still known for his honesty, righteousness, justice, and good morals, and for abandoning immoral acts and injustice. Every description is reprehensible, and it is recognized as such by all who knew it before the prophecy, and from those who believed in it, and from those who disbelieved after the prophecy, no. He knows something that he is criticized for; Neither in his words, nor in his actions, nor in his morals, nor was there ever a lie, nor injustice, nor indecency tried against him, and his character and image were He is one of the most complete forms, the most complete, and the most comprehensive of the beauties that indicate his perfection. He was an illiterate person from an illiterate people who did not know what he or they were. The People of the Book know it:

He studied the Torah and the Gospel, and he did not read anything about people’s knowledge, nor did he sit with its people, nor did he claim prophethood until God had completed forty years for him. Then he brought something that was the most amazing and greatest of all things, and with words the likes of which the ancients and others had never heard of, and he informed us of a matter that had never happened. In his country and his people, who knows someone like him?

Then the followers of the prophets followed him while they were weak people, and the people of leadership rejected him and were hostile to him, and they sought to destroy him and the destruction of those who followed him. In every way, as the disbelievers used to do to the prophets and their followers, and those who followed him did not follow him out of desire or fear.

For he did not have money to give them, nor positions to give them, nor did he have a sword. Rather, the sword, money, and prestige were with his enemies. They harmed his followers with all kinds of harm, and they are patient and seek reward, and do not turn away from their religion because of the sweetness that has mixed with their hearts. Faith and knowledge.

The Arabs used to make pilgrimage to Mecca since the time of Abraham, and the Arab tribes would gather during the season, and he would go out to them and convey the message to them. And they call them to God, patient with what he meets of the liars of the liar, the cruelty of the treacherous, and the turning away of the one who turns away, until he meets with the people of Yathrib, and they were neighbors of the Jews who had heard news of him from them, and they knew him, so when he called them, they knew that he was the expected prophet whom you were telling them about. The Jews, and they had heard from his news what they knew of his status, for his matter had spread, and appeared within a few ten years, so they believed. With it, they pledged allegiance to him on his migration and the migration of his companions to their country, and on jihad with him, so he and those who followed him migrated to Medina, and with it The Muhajireen and Ansar, none of them believed out of worldly desire or out of fear, except for a few of the Ansar who outwardly converted to Islam, and then Some of them converted to Islam well, then they were allowed to engage in jihad, then they were ordered to do it, and they continued to follow the command of God in the most perfect way, and did it with complete honesty. And justice and loyalty, not a single lie was committed against him, nor did he do injustice to anyone, nor did he betray anyone. Rather, he was the most truthful and just of people. And he fulfilled his covenant with them, even though the circumstances changed for him, such as war and peace, security and fear, wealth and poverty, scarcity and abundance, and he appeared. Sometimes against the enemy and sometimes against the enemy, and it is

- Accordingly - necessary to complete the paths and complete them, until the call appeared in all the Arab lands that were filled with the worship of Idols, and from the reports of soothsayers, and the obedience of created beings in disbelief in the Creator, and the shedding of forbidden blood, and the severing of family ties, they do not know Hereafter, and there will be no return, so they became the most knowledgeable people on earth, the most pious, the most just, and the best of them, so much so that when the Christians saw them - when they came to the Levant - They said:

Those who accompanied Christ were not better than these, and these are the effects of their knowledge and work on earth, and the effects of others. Wise people know the difference. Between the two things.

And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and with the emergence of his authority, and the people’s obedience to him, and their submission to him over lives and wealth, he died, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. He greeted and did not leave behind a dirham, a dinar, a sheep, or a camel of his own, except for his mule, his weapon, and his armor, mortgaged to a Jew for thirty saa’s of He bought barley for his family, and he had property in his hand from which he spent on its family, and the rest he spent in the interests of the Muslims, so he ruled that he did not It is inherited and his heirs do not take anything from that.

And He is at all times the wonders of signs and miracles of miracles that are too long to describe, and He tells them the news of what has been and what has happened. He is, and he commands them to do what is right and forbids them what is wrong, and he makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the evil ones, and he legislates the Shari’a in all things. After a while, until God completed His religion with which He was sent, and His law came to be the most perfect law. There is no evil that minds know to be evil except that He forbade it. He did not command anything, and it was said, “I wish he had not commanded it.” Nor did He forbid anything, and it was said. I wish he had not forbidden it, and made lawful the good things and not forbidden any of them as they were forbidden in the law of others, and forbidden the bad things and not made lawful any of them as Others made it permissible, and combined the virtues of what the nations are upon, so no type of news about God and His angels is mentioned in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms. And about the Last Day, he brought it in the most complete manner, and told of things that are not in the books.
There is nothing in the Scriptures that enjoins justice, decrees virtue, recommends virtues, or encourages good deeds except that He brought it and what is best. From him.

If the intelligent person looks at the acts of worship that he has prescribed, and the acts of worship of other nations, their virtue and superiority will become clear, and the same applies to the limits set. And the rulings, and all other laws.

And his nation is the most perfect of nations in every virtue. If their knowledge is measured against the knowledge of other nations, the virtue of their knowledge becomes apparent, even if their religion is measured. And their worship and obedience to God in comparison with others makes it clear that they are more pious than others, and when their courage and struggle in the path of God is measured And their patience in the face of hardships in the name of God, shows that they are the greatest in striving and the bravest of hearts, and when their generosity, generosity, and tolerance are measured themselves to others, it became clear that they were more generous and generous than others, and they obtained these virtues from him, and from him they learned them, and he is the one who He commanded them to do it, because before him they had not followed a book that he came to complete, just as Christ came to complete the law of the Torah.

The virtues of the followers of Christ and their knowledge were some of them from the Torah, some of them from the Psalms, some of them from prophecies, and some of them from Christ, and some of them after him, such as the disciples, and they sought help from the words of philosophers and others until they entered - when they changed the religion of Christ - into the religion of Christ is one of the things of the infidels that are contrary to the religion of Christ.

As for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they did not read a book before him. Rather, most of them did not believe in Moses, Jesus, David, and the Torah. And the Gospel and the Psalms except on his part, for he is the one who commanded them to believe in all the prophets, and to acknowledge all the books revealed from With God, and He forbade them from separating between any of the Messengers, so God Almighty said in the Book that He brought:

{Say, “We believe in God and in what was revealed to us, and what was sent down to Abraham, and Ishmael, and Isaac, and Jacob, and the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what The prophets were given from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and to Him we submit.} [Al-Baqarah: 136] (136) {And if they believe in the like of what you have believed in, then it is true. They are guided, and if they turn away, then they are only in discord, so Allah will suffice you for them, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing” [Al-Baqarah: 137].

And God Almighty said: {The Messenger believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers are each who believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between anyone. Of His messengers, and they said, “We have heard and obeyed. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the return.” Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden as You placed upon those before us. Our Lord, nor You burden us with what we cannot bear, and pardon us, and forgive us, and have mercy on us, You are our Master, so help us against the disbelieving people} [Al-Baqarah: 285-286].

And his nation does not permit taking anything from the religion other than what it brought, nor do they innovate an innovation for which God has sent down no authority. They legislate from religion what God has not permitted.

But what he narrated to them of the news of the prophets and their nations, they took heed of it, and what the People of the Book narrated to them was in agreement with what they had. They believed him, and as long as they did not know whether he was truthful or a lie, they abstained from him, and they did not know that he was false, they disbelieved him, and whoever introduces into religion what is not from it. The philosophers of India, Persians, Greece, or others, were - according to them - people of atheism and innovation, and this is the religion that The Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who followed him, and he is the one who is the Imams of the religion, who have a truthful tongue among the nation. The community of Muslims and their common people are upon it, and whoever deviates from that will be reprehensible and rejected by the community, and this is the doctrine of the Sunnis. And the group of people who will appear until the Hour comes, about whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
“A group of my nation will continue to adhere to the truth. They will not be harmed by those who oppose them nor by those who abandon them, until the Hour comes.”
Some Muslims have disputed, even though they agreed on this principle, which is the religion of the Messengers in general, and the religion of Muhammad in particular.

And whoever differs from this principle is - according to them - a reprehensible atheist. They are not like the Christians who invented a religion established by their greatest scholars. And their worshipers, and their kings fought against it, and their masses embraced it, and it is an invented religion that is not the religion of Christ, nor the religion of other prophets.

And God - Glory be to Him, the Most High - sent His messengers with useful knowledge and righteous deeds, so whoever follows the messengers will attain happiness in this world and the hereafter. Only those who fell short in following the prophets in knowledge and deed entered into innovations.
And when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with guidance and the religion of truth, the Muslims, his nation, received that from him.

The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, acquired every beneficial knowledge and good deed from their Prophet, despite what appears to every rational person: that his nation The most perfect of nations in all scientific and practical virtues, and it is known that every perfection in the learned branch is from the original that teaches. This necessitates that he was the most complete of people in knowledge and religion, and these matters necessitate the necessary knowledge that he was truthful in his saying: {Indeed, I am a Messenger May God bless you all} [Al-A’raf: 158].

He was not a liar and a slanderer, for this saying can only be said by someone who is among the best and most perfect of people if he is truthful, or he is of evil. People and the most despicable of them if he is a liar.

What was mentioned about the perfection of his knowledge and religion contradicts evil, malice and ignorance, so it is clear that he is characterized by the utmost perfection in knowledge and religion. This necessitates that he was truthful in his saying: “Indeed, I am the Messenger of God” [Al-A’raf: 158].

Because the one who was not truthful must either be lying intentionally or wrong. The first means that he was unjust and deceitful. The second: It implies that he was ignorant and lost, and the perfection of his knowledge contradicted his ignorance, and the perfection of his religion contradicted intentional lying. Knowledge of his attributes necessitates knowledge that he was not lying intentionally, and was not ignorant and would lie without knowledge. If this is not the case, And that made it clear that he was truthful, knowing that he was truthful; For this reason, God exalted him from these two matters, saying:
{And the star, when it desires - your companion has never gone astray or gone astray - and it does not speak from desire - it is only a revelation revealed.} [An-Najm: 1-4].

And God Almighty said about the angel with whom He brought: {Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger - possessed of power and established by the Owner of the Throne - obedient and trustworthy} [Al-Takwir: 19-21].
Then he said about it: {And no madman accompanies you - and he has seen it on the clear horizon - and he is not over the unseen with worry} [Al-Takwir: 22-24].

That is: by an accuser or a miser, such as one who does not teach except with a reward, or to one who honors him: {And it is not the word of an accursed Satan - so where will you go - if... It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds} [Al-Takwir: 25-27].

And the Almighty said: {And indeed it is a revelation of the Lord of the worlds - the Faithful Spirit has sent it down - to your heart that you may be among the warners - in a clear Arabic language} [Al-Shu’ara’: 192 - 195].
To his saying: {Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend - upon whom do they descend upon every sinful avatar? 223].

Glory be to Him has made it clear that Satan only descends upon whomever suits him in order to achieve his purpose, for Satan intends evil: which is lying. And immorality, and it does not mean honesty and justice, it should only be associated with one in which there is lying, either intentionally or by mistake, for error in religion is one who Satan as well, as Ibn Masoud said - when he was asked about an issue -: “I say about it in my opinion, so if it is right then it is from God, and if it is wrong It is from me and from Satan, and God and His Messenger are free from it.”

The Messenger is innocent of Satan descending upon him intentionally or accidentally, unlike someone other than the Messenger, for he may make a mistake, and his mistake is of Satan, even if his mistake is forgiven, then if no news is known to him that he informs of, then he is mistaken, and no matter he commanded is in it. An immoral person, it was known that Satan had not descended upon him, but rather that a noble angel had descended upon him. That is why he said in the other verse on the authority of the Prophet: {Indeed, it is the saying of a noble Messenger - and it is not the saying of a poet - Little do you believe - nor the saying of a soothsayer. - Little do you remember - a revelation from the Lord of the worlds} [Al-Haqqah: 40-43].

chapters.title: A chapter on people’s transmission of his attributes, peace be upon him, that indicate his perfection
paragraphs: [Chapter: People’s transmission of his attributes, peace be upon him, that indicate his perfection]
People have copied his apparent qualities that indicate his perfection, and they have copied his morals, such as his forbearance, courage, generosity, asceticism, and so on. We mention some of that.

In the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Al-Baraa bin Aazib, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the best of people in face, and the best of character, not “By the long one, nor by the short one.”
And about him, he said: “He was as tall as his shoulders, his hair was as high as the lobes of his ears, and he was wearing a red robe. I have never seen anything better than him.”
And in Al-Bukhari: Al-Baraa was asked: “Was the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, like a sword?” He said: “No, but like the moon.”

And in the two Sahih books, from the hadith of Ka’b bin Malik, he said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was happy, his face would shine, to the point that it was like a piece of the moon.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a large head and feet. I had never seen him before him or After him there was the same thing, and the palms were spread out as large as the hands.”
“He was asked about his hair, and he said: “It was a man’s hair, neither curly nor straight, between his ears and his neck.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, he said: “The Messenger of God had a weak mouth, narrow eyes, and weak heels.” Simak bin Harb explained it, saying: “The mouth is wide, the eye is long, and the flesh of the heel is small.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Anas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was neither tall nor short, nor white and albino.” Nor by man, nor by curly cats, nor by tribes.”

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a bright complexion, as if his veins were pearls. When he walked, he would stoop, and he would not “I have never touched a brocade or silk softer than the palm of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor have I smelled musk or amber better than the scent of the Messenger of God.”
May God bless him and grant him peace.”

Al-Darimi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to open the two halves. When he spoke, light would be seen coming out of Its doubles.

It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “I have not seen anyone more sincere, more generous, more courageous, or more enlightened than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.”

On the authority of Anas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon us and said, ‘He was with us,’ and he sweated, and my mother came with a bottle and began to remove the sweat.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke up and said: Umm Sulaim, what are you doing? She said: This is your sweat, we will put it in it! “Our goodness, and it is better than good things.” They included it in the two Sahih books.

Al-Darimi narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not take a road and someone would follow him, unless he knew that he had taken it from... “The goodness of his sweat.”

And in the famous hadith of Umm Ma’abad, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by her during the migration, he and Abu Bakr, his master, and their guide, Her husband came and said: Describe him to me, O Umm Ma’abad. She said: “I saw a man who appeared to be very simple, with good logic, a gentleman, and neither vulgar nor gossip. “It is as if the string’s beads are descending.”

Abu Zur’ah narrated, “On the authority of Muhammad bin Ammar bin Yasser, she said: I said to Al-Rabi’ bint Mu’awiz bin Afra: Describe for us the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He greeted him, and she said: “My son, if you saw him, you would see the sun rising.”

And in the two Sahihs, “On the authority of Anas, he said: “The Messenger of God was the best of people, the most generous of people, and he was the bravest of people. The people of Medina were terrified.” One night, people set out before the sound, and the Messenger of God met them returning. He had preceded them to the sound, and he had learned the news, and he was on the verge of A horse belonging to Abu Talha, naked with a sword around his neck, and he was saying: You will not be heeded, and he said: “We found him by the sea.” The horse had been slow before that, so it did not return. »

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the most generous of people with goodness, and he was the most generous in Ramadan.” When Gabriel meets him and he studies the Qur’an with him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is more generous with goodness than a blowing wind.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Al-Baraa bin Azib, he said: “When the battle became red, we would protect ourselves from it, and the bravest among us is the one who fights against it (meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace). May God bless him and grant him peace.

“On the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, he said: “On the Day of Badr, we feared the polytheists of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was the most powerful of people. “No one is closer to the enemy than him.” Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it with an authentic chain of transmission.

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas, he said: “I served the Messenger of God for ten years, and by God, he never said to me (‘fa’), nor did he say to me for anything: Why did you do such-and-such?” And will you do this? .

And in a narration in the two Sahihs as well, he said: “I served him when he was traveling or at home, and by God he never said to me for anything I did: ‘Why did you do this like this?’” For something I did not do: Why did you not do this like this? He was the best of people.”
And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Jabir, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never asked anything and he said: No.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Anas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace upon Islam, was never asked for anything but he gave it to him. He said: Then a man came to him.” So he gave him sheep between two mountains, so he returned to his people and said: O my people, submit to Islam, for Muhammad gives the gift of one who does not fear poverty.

And in the two Sahih books on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was more shy than a virgin in her private room. He hated something that we recognized in his face.”
And in the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned, he said: “He was neither obscene nor obscene.”

Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not curse, commit adultery, or curse. He used to say to one of us when... “Al-Mu’tabah: He has no dust on his forehead.”

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never given a choice between two matters unless he chose the easier of the two, unless... It would be a sin, for if it was a sin he would keep people away from it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never avenged himself unless it was violated. “The sanctity of God.” .

On her authority, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never struck anything with his hand, neither a woman nor a servant, unless he was struggling in the cause of God. “Nothing has ever been done to him and he takes revenge on its owner, unless something of God’s prohibitions is violated and he takes revenge for God.”
Muslim narrated in his Sahih, “On her authority, she was asked about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: “His character was the Qur’an.”

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of Shu`bah, Abu Ishaq narrated to us, Abu Abdullah al-Jadali narrated to us, he said: “I heard Aisha, He asked her about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: “He was not obscene or indecent, nor did he make noise in the markets, and he did not reward with a bad deed, but he pardons and pardons, or forgives.” Abu Dawud doubted.
It was narrated by Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak on the two Sahih books.

And in the two Sahih books, “On the authority of Alqamah, he said: I asked Aisha: How was the work of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Was he singling out any of the days? She said: “No, his work was constant, and any of you could do what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, could not.”
Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Saad bin Hisham, “He asked Aisha, may God be pleased with her, about the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
She said: “Don’t you read the Qur’an?” He said: “Yes.” She said: “The creation of the Prophet of God is the Qur’an.”
And in Sahih Al-Hakim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was sent to perfect good morals.”

And in the two Sahih books, on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, he said: “The Messenger of God stood up until his feet swelled, and it was said: O Messenger of God, has not God forgiven you for your sins?” What progressed from your sin and what delayed? He said: Shall I not be a grateful servant?

And in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never criticized food. If he desired it, he ate it, otherwise he abandoned it.”

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Abu Sheikh Al-Asbahani narrated from “the hadith of Bahz bin Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, That his brother came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “My neighbors are for what they have taken.” Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and said: “The people They claim that you have forbidden wrongdoing, and then you are free from it.” He said: “Because I was doing that because it is against me and it is against them, leave it to him.” His neighbors.

Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: “There was no person more beloved to them than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. peace be upon him, and when they saw him they would not get up, because they knew of his hatred for that.” Narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi: Thana Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Humaid, on the authority of him.

Abu Nu`aym, Abu al-Sheikh, and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “Indeed, God sent to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a king of The angels were with Gabriel, and he said: The angel: “God gave him a choice between being a servant and being a king.”

A prophet, he said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel like a counselor, and Gabriel indicated with his hand: Be humble, so the Messenger of God said God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: “No, but I will be a prophet’s servant.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Al-Bukhari in his history.

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas, he said: “A Jewish boy was serving the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he fell ill, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him.” He said: Do you bear witness that there is no god but Allah? So the boy looked at his father, and his father said to him: “Obey Abul-Qasim.” So he submitted to Islam, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Praise be to God who He saved him from the fire through me.”

“And on the authority of Abu Hazim, that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, spoke to a man and he trembled, so the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to him: Take it easy, for I I am not a king, but I am the son of a woman from the Quraysh who used to eat kefid.” Narrated by Ibn al-Jawzi through chains of transmission, some of which are related to Ibn Masoud, Ibn al-Jawzi said: “It was narrated connected,” and the correct thing is to send it as mentioned above.

And in the Sahih, on the authority of Anas: “A woman had something on her mind. She said: O Messenger of God, I have a need of you.” He said: “O mother of so-and-so, take any “Whichever way you want, stay on it until I stay with you.” So he left with her, conversing with her until she fulfilled her need. “Narrated by Muslim.

“And on the authority of Anas, he said: “The female slave of the people of Medina used to take the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and use him to attend to her needs. Until you finish, then he returns.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari in Al-Adab.
It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Awfa that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to walk with the widow and the poor person and fulfill their needs.”

On his authority, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to make a lot of dhikr and talk less, lengthen the prayer, shorten the sermon, and would not stop short of his sermon. That he should walk with the servant or with the widow, until he has finished their needs.” Narrated by Al-Darimi and Al-Hakim in his Sahih.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to ride a donkey, wear wool, and respond to invitations.” Mamluk, and I saw him on the Day of Khaybar riding a donkey with a fibre’s muzzle.”
Muslim narrated in his Sahih “On the authority of Anas, he said: “I have not seen anyone more merciful to my family than the Messenger of God.”
Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of him, saying, “The Messenger of God passed by some boys and greeted them.”
Ibn Abbas narrated, saying: “The Messenger of God used to sit on the ground, eat on the ground, arrest the sheep, and respond to the invitations of the king.” .

“And on the authority of Qudamah bin Abdullah: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, riding a gray mule, neither beaten nor driven away, nor to thee.” Narrated by Abu Al-Sheikh.

“And on the authority of Aisha, she said: “I never saw the Messenger of God laughing, so that I could see his amusement. Rather, he was smiling, and whenever If he saw a cloud or a wind, he recognized his face, so I said: O Messenger of God, when people see clouds they rejoice, hoping that it will rain, and I will see you then. I saw that he saw the hatred on your face. He said: O Aisha, and what makes me believe that there will be a torment in which a people has been tortured with a wind, and it has come? The torment of a people, and he recited the Almighty’s saying: “And when they saw it spreading toward their valleys, they said, ‘This is a stream, raining on us.’” [Al-Ahqaf: 24] »
He included it in the two Sahih books.

And in the two Sahihs - also - “On the authority of Anas, he said: “I was walking with the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and he was wearing a thick, thick Najran cloak, and it overtook him. A Bedouin, and his robe was pulled tightly together, until I looked at the page of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which had been touched by a footnote. He was cold because of his extreme severity, then he said: O Muhammad, pass me some of God’s wealth that you have. He said: Then the Messenger of God turned to him and he laughed, then he ordered He has a gift.”

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir bin Samurah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not get up from the place where he was praying until the When the sun rose, he would rise, and they would talk about pre-Islamic times, and they would laugh and he would smile.”
And in another authentic narration: “He was silent for a long time, laughed little, and his companions would often ask him about poetry or any of their affairs. They laugh and he smiles.”

And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, Al-Aswad asked her: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do in His family? She said: “He was doing his family’s job - meaning serving his family - so when prayer came, he would go out.”
And from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwa.
He said: “A man asked Aisha: Was he working at home? She said: He would mend his shoes, sew his clothes, and work in his house as any of you would work in his house.

Al-Tayalisi narrated: Shu’bah told us, Al-A’war told us, he said: I heard Anas say: “The Messenger of God used to ride a donkey, wear wool, and bring The summons of the Mamluk, and I saw him on the Day of Khaybar on a donkey whose muzzle was made of fibre.”
Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Anas, who said: “I have never seen anyone more merciful to family than the Messenger of God.”
Al-Bukhari narrated that he said: “The Messenger of God passed by some boys and greeted them.”

And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not satisfied for three days with whole wheat bread.” successively, until he went on his way.”

On her authority, she said: “We, the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pass by the crescent moon and the crescent moon. We would not light a fire for food, except dates and water. The people of the Ansar attacked us, and the people of each house would send the meat of their sheep to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, drinks from that milk.” They included it in the two Sahih books.
And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, “Anas said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never saw a flaky loaf until he joined God, nor did he see a flaky sheep.” Never with his own eyes.

And in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of him: “The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, did not eat in private, nor in a desert place, nor did he have any bread that was unleavened.” So he was told: What were they eating? He said: “On the journey.”

And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Omar Ibn Al-Khattab: He delivered a sermon and mentioned what was revealed to the people, and he said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He writhes with hunger all day long, finding nothing of the dung to fill his stomach.

And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Anas: “He went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with barley bread and a generous sacrifice, and he pledged his armor.” With a Jew, he took barley for his family, and I heard him say: The family of Muhammad has not had a saa’ of wheat nor a saa’ of grain, and on that day they will Nine verses.
And it is narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The bed of the Messenger of God was made of human beings stuffed with fiber.”

And in Sahih Muslim, from “the hadith of Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him - when he mentioned the Messenger of God’s seclusion from his wives - he said: “So I went to the Messenger of God God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was in his closet, and behold, he was lying on a mat. He brought his garment to him and sat down, and behold, the mat had affected Next to him, and I turned my eyes around his house and did not find anything that averted the sight except a handful of barley and a handful of qarth about the two sa'is, and when he woke up Hanging, my eyes lit up, and the Messenger of God said: What makes you cry, Ibn Al-Khattab? I said:

O Messenger of God, why should I not cry when you are the elite of God and His Messenger and the best of His creation, and this is your treasury, and these foreigners are Chosroes And Caesar in the fruits and rivers! He said: Are you in doubt, Ibn Al-Khattab? ! These are a people whose good deeds have been hastened for them in their life of this world, and in a narration or whatever. Are you satisfied that this world is theirs, and the Hereafter is ours? He said: Yes, he said: Praise be to God Almighty. He said: “I said: I ask forgiveness from God.”

And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, make the livelihood of the family of Muhammad a source of sustenance.”

Al-Tayalisi narrated with an authentic chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: “The Prophet lay down on a mat, and the mat affected his skin, so I started wiping it.” And I say: “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God. Have you not given us permission to spread something for you that will protect you from it, so that you can sleep on it?” He said: “I have nothing to do with the world. I and the world are nothing but like a rider who took shade under a tree, then he went away and left it.”
Al-Hakim narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Omar entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned something similar.

And in Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, performed Hajj on shabby saddlebags and velvet,” and Al-Bukhari also narrated it on the authority of Anas in (The Book of Hajj) said: “Anas performed Hajj on a shabby saddlebag, and he was not stingy. It happened that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj on a saddlebag. “And she was his companion.”

And in Sahih Al-Hakim on the authority of Anas: “The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, wore coarse, ate coarse, wore wool, and wore leather. It was said to Al-Hasan: What is rough? He said: “Barley is thick, it was not sweetened except with a sip of water.”
